`isPrivate` the documents select.

**How we found it**: the client-go run of `cmd/audit_graphql_shapes`, issue
1022.

**Effort**: small: four fields and their tests.

### DependencyListExport carries four of the eight fields GitLab sends

- **Reported**: no. It was to go into the joint merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  with the other struct gaps of this register; that merge request was closed
  unmerged on 2026-10-21, so it goes out in a small merge request on its
  topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.15.0 carries the four fields.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `dependency.export_create` and `dependency.export_get`
  (`internal/tools/dependencies/dependencies.go`) call the SDK under
  `gitlabclient.WithResponseCapture` (ADR-0021) and read `status`,
  `export_type`, `send_email` and `expires_at` from the captured answer. It
  retires when the struct models them.

**Where**: `dependency_list_export.go`, `DependencyListExport`, at v3.15.0,
which `CreateDependencyListExport` and `GetDependencyListExport` decode into.

**What**: GitLab renders a dependency list export through
`API::Entities::DependencyListExport`, which exposes `id`, `status` (the
state's name: `created`, `running`, `finished` or `failed`), `has_finished`,
`export_type`, `send_email`, `expires_at`, `self` and `download`. The struct
models `id`, `has_finished`, `self` and `download`. The status is the field a
caller polls on, and the one this server's own hints told a model to wait
for, while the output it was handed had only the boolean.

**How we found it**: issue 1307. GitLab's generated record carries no
response entity for the `dependency_list_exports` routes, so R-PATH never
compared them; the entity itself is in `gitlab-api-live.json`.

**Effort**: small: four fields and a decoding test.

### The model package file path segment cannot be omitted

- **Reported**: no. It was to go into the joint merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  with the other gaps of this register; that merge request was closed
  unmerged on 2026-10-21, so it goes out in a small merge request on its
  topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.15.0 writes the segment.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `model_registry.download`
  (`internal/tools/modelregistry/model_registry.go`) sends a request of its own
  for a file at the package root (`downloadFromPackageRoot`, on the route
  `rootFilePath` builds) and calls the SDK for a file in a directory. It
  retires when the method can leave the path out.

**Where**: `model_registry.go`, `DownloadMachineLearningModelPackage`, at
v3.15.0, whose route is `projects/%s/packages/ml_models/%s/files/%s/%s` with
the path escaped into the third placeholder whatever its value.

**What**: GitLab declares the route as
`:id/packages/ml_models/:model_version_id/files/(*path/):file_name`
(`lib/api/ml_model_packages.rb`), the path an optional group, and looks the
file up by the path and the file name joined. A file uploaded at the root of a
model version's package has no path, and the method cannot ask for one: an
empty path is sent as `files//model.bin` and `.` as `files/./model.bin`.
Against GitLab 19.4.2, through its nginx and straight at Workhorse's socket,
`files/model.bin` and `files//model.bin` answer 200 and `files/./model.bin`
answers 404 `Not found`, the package's own not-found, since the file looked up
is `./model.bin`. The empty segment works by the tolerance of the router rather
than by the route's declaration, and the one spelling a caller would reach for
to name the root does not work at all.

**How we found it**: issue 1318. This server required the path, so a file at
the root of a package could not be downloaded; the root form was settled by a
live check against a CE 19.4.2 on 2026-10-12, which uploaded one file at the
root and one nested to a private project's model version and asked for both
in every spelling.

**Effort**: small: an option that drops the segment, or a path argument the
method leaves out when it is empty, and a routing test.

### A measure GitLab sends as null decodes as 0

- **Reported**: no. It was to go into the joint merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  with the other struct gaps of this register; that merge request was closed
  unmerged on 2026-10-21, so it goes out in a small merge request on its
  topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, decodes every one of
  them as a number, as v3.15.0 did, and v3.40.0 still does.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes, for every one of these but a deployable's. Each
  handler that presents one of them calls the SDK under
  `gitlabclient.WithResponseCapture` (ADR-0021) and reads the value from the
  captured answer as a pointer: `toolutil.PipelineMeasures` (through
  `toolutil.PipelineExtra` for a pipeline read or triggered),
  `toolutil.JobMeasures` and `toolutil.CapturedJob`/`CapturedJobs` for the
  pipeline, trigger, job and bridge handlers and the job resources (the
  bridge list through `toolutil.CapturedBridges`, on its `trigger_jobs` and
  `bridges` routes alike), the
  measures of a merge request's head pipeline through
  `toolutil.MergeRequestExtra`, a project board's weight scope through
  `toolutil.BoardExtra`, and a reader of its own in `dorametrics`,
  `mergetrains` and `resourceevents`. A deployable's coverage and duration,
  on a deployment and on an environment's last deployment, are still read
  from client-go and left out at 0, so they show no false 0 and drop a
  measured one. It retires when the structs carry pointers. A milestone's
  burndown events need none of this: client-go already decodes their weight
  as a pointer. A group board's weight scope is not a case of this row at
  v3.30.0, where `GroupIssueBoard` declares no weight at all
  ([row 101](#the-board-structs-miss-keys-gitlab-sends-on-a-board-and-its-lists)'s
  gap), and `toolutil.GroupBoardExtra` reads it off the captured response as
  a pointer. It becomes one from v3.39.0, whose `GroupIssueBoard.Weight`,
  added by
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3085](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3085),
  ours, is an `int64` like `IssueBoard.Weight`, so the pointer read stays
  when row 101's other keys retire.

**Where**: at v3.15.0 and unchanged at v3.30.0, `DORAMetric.Value`
(`float64`, `dora_metrics.go`), `Pipeline.Duration` and
`Pipeline.QueuedDuration` (`int64`, `pipelines.go`), `Job`, `Bridge` and
`TriggerJob` (added in v3.24.0 for the `trigger_jobs` route, field for field
`Bridge`) `Duration`, `QueuedDuration` and `Coverage` (`float64`,
`jobs.go`), `DeploymentDeployable.Duration` and `Coverage` (`float64`,
`deployments.go`), `MergeTrain.Duration` (`int64`, `merge_trains.go`),
`IssueBoard.Weight` (`int64`, `boards.go`) and `WeightEvent.Weight` (`int64`,
`resource_weight_events.go`). Two more came later: `UserPipeline.Duration`
and `QueuedDuration` (`int64`, `pipelines.go`, from v3.37.0, decoded by
`ListUserPipelines`, which no handler here calls) and `GroupIssueBoard.Weight` (`int64`, `group_boards.go`,
from v3.39.0). All of them are still so at v3.40.0.

**What**: GitLab sends each of these as `null` when there is nothing to
measure: a DORA period with no deployments to take a median over (the lead
time and time to restore are a `PERCENTILE_CONT` over no rows), a pipeline or
job that never ran (created, skipped, or a manual job nobody played), a job
that reported no coverage, a merge train car whose train has not run, a
weight event that took the weight away, and a board with no weight scope.
The structs decode that `null` as the
type's zero, so a project with no measurable incidents reads as restoring
service in zero seconds, the best value there is, and a manual job reads as
one that ran for no time at all. A real 0 is also sent (a deployment
frequency of 0, a job measured at 0% coverage, a weight set to 0), so neither
the zero nor `omitempty` can tell the two apart; only a pointer can.

**How we found it**: issue 1309, reproduced against GitLab EE with a skipped
pipeline, a manual job and the DORA endpoints of a project with no
deployments.

**Effort**: small: pointer fields and their decoding tests, a breaking type
change that a major release of client-go carries.

### Block, unblock and deactivate drop the answer that says whether anything changed

- **Reported**: no. It was to go into the joint merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  with the other gaps of this register; that merge request was closed
  unmerged on 2026-10-21, so it goes out in a small merge request on its
  topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.15.0 decodes none of the three answers.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `user.block`, `user.unblock` and `user.deactivate`
  call the SDK under `gitlabclient.WithResponseCapture` (ADR-0021) and read
  the answer as a `*bool` (`stateChangeOutput` in
  `internal/tools/users/user_admin.go`): `true` is a change, and `false` or
  `null` is reported as one that did not happen, with the state the user was
  probably in. It retires when the methods return the answer.

**Where**: at v3.15.0, `UsersService.BlockUser`, `UnblockUser` and
`DeactivateUser` (`users.go`), each of which decodes into `none` and returns
only the `*Response` and an error chosen from the status code.

**What**: GitLab answers `POST /users/:id/block`, `/unblock` and
`/deactivate` with 201 whether or not it changed the user's state, and says
which in the body: `true` when it did, `false` or `null` when it did not. An
unblock of a user who is not blocked answers `false`, and a block of a user
already blocked and a second deactivate answer `null`. The methods return no
value, so a caller is told 201 and nothing else, and a state change that did
not happen reads as one that did. The other state changes (`activate`, `ban`,
`unban`, `approve`, `reject`) refuse a no-op with a 4xx or answer an object,
so the status already tells their outcome.

**How we found it**: issue 1327, reproduced against GitLab EE in the
`test/e2e` Docker stack with an administrator token.

**Effort**: small: return the decoded bool, a signature change that a major
release of client-go carries, with a test per answer.

### UpdateWorkItemOptions cannot remove a reference, a date or the health status

- **Reported**: no. It belonged with the work item commits of the joint merge
  request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  and was never in it; that merge request was closed unmerged on 2026-10-21,
  so it goes out with the work item commits in a small merge request on their
  topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.17.0 builds the input the same way.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `toolutil.ApplyWorkItemWidgets` reads the milestone,
  parent, iteration, start date, due date and health status of an update
  under the clearing convention every update here follows (0 removes a
  reference, "" removes a date or the health status) and returns a request
  option that writes null into the matching widget of the `workItemUpdate`
  input client-go has encoded, beside whatever else the update sets. It
  leaves alone the global-ID lookup client-go sends first with the same
  options. `issue.work_item_update` and `group.epic_update` use it. It
  retires when the option struct can express a removal.

**Where**: `workitems.go`, `UpdateWorkItemOptions.wrap` and the
`workItemWidget*InputGQL` structs it fills.

**What**: `wrap` turns every reference it is handed into a global ID, so a
milestone, parent or iteration of 0 reaches GitLab as
`gid://gitlab/Milestone/0`, `gid://gitlab/WorkItem/0` or
`gid://gitlab/Iteration/0`, which GitLab answers with "No object found". The
start and due dates, the health status and the three references are each
carried by a pointer whose widget field is tagged `omitempty`, so there is no
value of the option struct that makes the widget carry null, and null is how
GitLab's schema removes each of them (`WorkItemWidgetHierarchyUpdateInput`
documents `parentId` as "Use `null` to remove the association"; the
milestone, iteration, start and due date and health status inputs are all
nullable). A caller of client-go can therefore set any of these and remove
none.

The replacement of the closed draft that moved this service to REST,
[gitlab-org/api/client-go!3078](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3078),
adds a separate REST service and leaves the GraphQL one and its documents as
they are, so the workaround reads the same request after it merges.

**How we found it**: issue 1303, from a work item whose iteration, parent and
due date could not be removed through `issue.work_item_update`, and issue
1302, from the epic dates and health status `group.epic_update` could not
remove.

**Effort**: small to medium: a removal per field the option struct can say,
as a `Nullable` type or a set of `Clear` flags, which is a choice of API for
the maintainers.

### ListAuditEventsOptions models neither entity filter the instance list takes

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.17.0 carries the same struct.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `audit_event.list_instance` takes `entity_type` and
  `entity_id` and adds them to the query client-go has encoded through a
  request option of its own (`entityFilter` in
  `internal/tools/auditevents/audit_events.go`), and refuses an `entity_id`
  without an `entity_type` before any request, as GitLab would. It retires
  when the struct carries both fields.

**Where**: `audit_events.go`, `ListAuditEventsOptions`, which
`ListInstanceAuditEvents` sends to `GET /audit_events` and the group and
project lists to their own routes.

**What**: the struct carries the page, `created_after` and `created_before`
and nothing else, while the instance route
(`ee/lib/api/audit_events.rb`) also takes `entity_type`, one of `Project`,
`User`, `Group` and `Gitlab::Audit::InstanceScope`, and `entity_id`, which
requires `entity_type` beside it. Without them an administrator after one
project's or one user's trail has to page through every event of the
instance. The group and project routes take neither, since the entity is in
their path, so one struct serving all three is right about them and short
only for the instance list.

**How we found it**: issue 1308. The 403 hint of `audit_event.list_instance`
told a caller without administrator access to narrow the list by entity,
which the tool could not do.

**Effort**: small: two fields with `url` tags, and a test that each reaches
the query.

### UpdateReleaseOptions sends the title and the notes as null on every partial update

- **Reported**: no. It belonged with the option struct commits of the joint
  merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  and was never in it; that merge request was closed unmerged on 2026-10-21,
  so it goes out with the option struct commits in a small merge request on
  their topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `release.update` passes `toolutil.EditJSONBody`, a
  request option that takes the `name` and `description` keys out of the
  JSON body client-go encoded whenever the caller did not set them, so an
  update of the release date or the milestones sends neither. It retires
  when both fields carry `omitempty`.

**Where**: `releases.go`, `UpdateReleaseOptions`, which `UpdateRelease`
sends to `PUT /projects/:id/releases/:tag_name`. At v3.15.0 its `Name` and
`Description` are tagged `json:"name"` and `json:"description"`, while
`CreateReleaseOptions` beside it tags both `omitempty`.

**What**: a nil pointer without `omitempty` is written as `null`, so every
partial update carries `"name":null,"description":null`. The route hands
`declared_params(include_missing: false)` to `Releases::UpdateService`,
which keeps a parameter sent as null and runs `release.update(params)`, and
`Release#name` reads `read_attribute(:name) || tag`. A caller who changes
only `released_at` or the milestones therefore erases the release notes and
renames the release to its tag, and is told the update succeeded. GitLab,
called directly with only the date, leaves both untouched.

**How we found it**: issue 1305, from a release whose notes vanished after
an update of its date. The always-sent check of R-PATH did not report it,
because the request inventory recorded the route with the fixture's tag in
it (`/releases/v1.0.0`, `/releases/v1.2.0`), which joined nothing; the test
recorder now names the segment after `releases` `:tag_name`, the way the
live record does, so the check reaches the route once the inventory is
regenerated.

**Effort**: small: `omitempty` on both halves of two tags, and a test that a
date-only update sends neither key.

### Eight update option structs cannot send the null or the empty list that clears a field

- **Reported**: no. It belonged with the option struct commits of the joint
  merge request,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063),
  and was never in it; that merge request was closed unmerged on 2026-10-21,
  so it goes out with the option struct commits in a small merge request on
  their topic.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.18.0 carries the same fields, and so do v3.29.0, which
  adds the eighth struct's field, and v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. Each handler reads the field as a pointer and passes
  `toolutil.EditJSONBody`, the request option that writes into the JSON body
  client-go encoded: `toolutil.NullWhenZero` records the key as null when the
  caller sent `""` or `0`, and the broadcast message update writes `[]` when
  the caller sent an empty list. `merge_request.update` does it for
  `merge_after` (`buildUpdateOpts` in
  `internal/tools/mergerequests/merge_requests.go`), where the caller's `""`
  goes out as null, and `TestUpdate_OptionalFields_ReachTheBody` holds the
  body. It retires field by field as each option can carry the value.

**Where**: eight option structs and the methods that send them, at v3.15.0
for the first seven and v3.29.0 for the eighth:

- `EditGroupMemberOptions.MemberRoleID` and
  `EditProjectMemberOptions.MemberRoleID`, `*int64` tagged `omitempty`, sent
  by `EditGroupMember` and `EditProjectMember`.
- `UpdateReleaseLinkOptions.FilePath` and `DirectAssetPath`, `*string`
  tagged `omitempty`, sent by `UpdateReleaseLink`.
- `UpdatePagesOptions.PagesPrimaryDomain`, `*string` tagged `omitempty`,
  sent by `UpdatePages`.
- `UpdateBroadcastMessageOptions.TargetAccessLevels`, a
  `[]AccessLevelValue` tagged `omitempty`, sent by `UpdateBroadcastMessage`.
- `UpdateAdminCompliancePolicySettingsOptions.CSPNamespaceID`, `*int64`
  tagged `omitempty`, sent by `UpdateCompliancePolicySettings`.
- `EditProjectOptions.MaxArtifactsSize` and `CIDeletePipelinesInSeconds`,
  `*int64` tagged `omitempty`, sent by `EditProject`.
- `UpdateMergeRequestOptions.MergeAfter`, a `*time.Time` tagged `omitempty`,
  sent by `UpdateMergeRequest`, which v3.29.0 added with
  `CreateMergeRequestOptions.MergeAfter` through another contributor's
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3128](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3128).

Beside them, `CreateGroupLabelOptions.Priority` and
`UpdateGroupLabelOptions.Priority` offer a priority that no group label
route takes.

**What**: each of these fields is one GitLab clears only with a value the
struct cannot hold. A nil pointer is left out and a pointer to `""` or `0` is
sent as written, while GitLab clears with null: a member's custom role
(`ee/app/services/ee/members/update_service.rb` removes it on an explicit
null, and refuses to change the access level while one is assigned), a
release link's paths (`app/models/releases/link.rb` refuses `""` through
`FILEPATH_REGEX`), the Pages primary domain (`lib/api/pages.rb` refuses a
value that is not one of the project's domains, and `""` is not), the
compliance policy namespace (the route requires the key, and on GitLab
19.4.2 `null` clears it while leaving the key out is answered 400), a
project's artifact size limit and pipeline retention (`app/models/project.rb`
validates `max_artifacts_size` above 0 and `app/models/project_ci_cd_setting.rb`
validates `delete_pipelines_in_seconds` at a day or more, both allowing nil,
which puts back the instance's limit and keeps pipelines for ever), and a
merge request's merge schedule (at `v19.5.0-ee`, lines 19 to 22 of
`app/services/merge_requests/update_service.rb` hand a `merge_after` the
request carries to `MergeRequests::UpdateMergeScheduleService`, whose lines
11 to 17 destroy the schedule for a blank value, and a `*time.Time` has no
blank value to send). A slice
tagged `omitempty` leaves an empty list out, and `[]` is what GitLab reads as
a broadcast message shown to every role. A caller of client-go can therefore
set each of these and clear none. The group label priority is the reverse:
neither `POST` nor `PUT /groups/:id/labels` declares one, and
`lib/api/helpers/label_helpers.rb` applies a priority to a project label
only, so the field is sent and does nothing.

**How we found it**: issue 1306 and its comments, from a member whose custom
role could not be removed (and whose access level could not change because
of it) through `group.group_member_edit`, and by reading the handlers the
clearing gate in `internal/tools/action_specs_test.go` reported once every
other field reached GitLab, the two project limits once the gate probed the
integer fields with 0 as well. The compliance policy half was measured on
GitLab 19.4.2 before the workaround was written; the project limits are read
from GitLab 19.4.1's models, not measured. The eighth came with the v3.29.0
pin, when `merge_request.update` began taking `merge_after` through the new
option, which can set a merge schedule and cannot remove one; it is read
from GitLab 19.5.0's services, not measured.

**Effort**: small to medium: a `Nullable` type on each pointer, or a set of
`Clear` flags, which is the same choice of API row 119 leaves to the
maintainers; the slice and the priority are one tag and one deletion.

### The issue statistics options type assignee_id as an integer

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.18.0 carries the same fields.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `toolutil.Int64UserIDFilter` reads the filter as a
  user ID, `None` or `Any`: an ID goes into the option as before, and a
  literal leaves the option nil and is written into the query client-go
  encoded through a request option. `issue.statistics_get`,
  `issue.statistics_get_group` and `issue.statistics_get_project` use it. It
  retires when the three fields take an `*AssigneeIDValue`.

**Where**: `issues_statistics.go`, the `AssigneeID` field of
`GetIssuesStatisticsOptions`, `GetGroupIssuesStatisticsOptions` and
`GetProjectIssuesStatisticsOptions`, each `*int64`, sent to
`GET /issues_statistics`, `GET /groups/:id/issues_statistics` and
`GET /projects/:id/issues_statistics`.

**What**: GitLab declares `assignee_id` on all three routes as an integer or
a string, and reads `None` as the issues nobody is assigned and `Any` as the
issues somebody is, as it does on the issue lists. client-go's list options
type the same field `*AssigneeIDValue`, built with `gl.AssigneeID`, which
takes a user ID or `gl.UserIDNone` and `gl.UserIDAny`; the statistics options
beside them take only a number. A caller of client-go can therefore count
the issues assigned to one user and cannot count the unassigned ones, which
is the question a triage count asks most.

**How we found it**: issue 1354, which widened `assignee_id` on the issue
and merge request lists to take `None` and `Any` and found that the three
statistics actions, which take the same filter, could not follow without a
request option of their own.

**Effort**: small: the type of three fields, the same change client-go made
on the list options.

### Three option structs carry a timestamp parameter as a date

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.17.0 carries the same types.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. The handlers read the input through
  `toolutil.ParseTimeField`, leave the option struct's field unset, and pass
  `toolutil.TimestampParam`, a request option that writes the instant given,
  in RFC 3339 with its offset, into the JSON body client-go encoded for a
  POST and into the query for a GET. `user.add_ssh_key`,
  `user.add_ssh_key_for_user`, `snippet.list_all`,
  `repository.changelog_add` and `repository.changelog_generate` use it, and
  their schemas publish the parameter as a `date-time`. It retires when the
  fields take a `*time.Time`.

**Where**: `users.go`, `AddSSHKeyOptions.ExpiresAt`, which `AddSSHKey` and
`AddSSHKeyForUser` send to `POST /user/keys` and `POST /users/:user_id/keys`;
`snippets.go`, `ListAllSnippetsOptions.CreatedAfter` and `CreatedBefore`, for
`GET /snippets/all`; and `repositories.go`, the `Date` of
`AddChangelogOptions` and `GenerateChangelogDataOptions`, for
`POST` and `GET /projects/:id/repository/changelog`. All five are `*ISOTime`
at v3.15.0 and v3.17.0.

**What**: GitLab declares each of these parameters `DateTime` (the live
record of 19.4.1 holds every one of them so), and `ISOTime` encodes as
`YYYY-MM-DD`, which Grape reads as midnight UTC. So a key asked to expire at
2026-12-31T23:00:00Z expires at the start of that day, 23 hours early, one
asked to expire later today is refused as already expired, and a
`created_before` of 2026-10-12T18:00:00Z excludes every snippet of that day
after midnight. The changelog date only titles the release with its day, so
the date there loses nothing a reader sees. `InvitesOptions.ExpiresAt` is the
same type for a `DateTime` parameter too, but a membership's expiry is a date
column, so it loses nothing either and is left out of this row.

**How we found it**: issue 1308, moving every date input of the catalog onto
one parser and checking each field it fills against the route it reaches.

**Effort**: small: the five fields become `*time.Time`, a breaking change for
callers that build the options, so it waits for a major version or a parallel
field.

### A nil SearchOptions panics in every search method but one

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below, with no issue first.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3139](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3139)
  ("fix(search): accept nil SearchOptions in every search method"), opened
  by this project's maintainer at 05:14 UTC on 2026-10-14.
- **Merged**: **yes, v3.22.1**. It merged at 21:32 UTC on 2026-10-14, and
  v3.22.1 is the first tag that carries it. This server pins v3.30.0, which
  does.
- **Blocking**: no. Every search action builds its options through
  `searchOpts` in `internal/tools/search/search.go`, which returns a
  non-nil `*gl.SearchOptions` even when no option is set, so no call of
  this server reaches the panic.
- **Workaround**: not needed, for the same reason.

**Where**: `search.go`. Every `SearchService` method builds its query with
`&searchOptions{SearchOptions: *opt, ...}`, and only `UsersByGroup` checks
`opt` for nil first; in the other 24 a nil pointer is dereferenced before any
request is built (`MergeRequestsByProject` at
[search.go line 171](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/blob/95be8ccfe9d53662afa790a886a17ad1754ddd4d/search.go#L171)).

**What**: a caller that passes no options, which the search API allows since
it needs only `scope` and `search` and every method fills both from its own
arguments, panics with a nil pointer dereference instead of sending the
request.

**How we found it**: reading client-go's search service, which this server's
search actions call; nothing here passes nil, so no failure of this server
led to it.

**Fix merged**: an unexported `newSearchOptions` helper copies the options
only when they are set, all 25 methods call it, and the nil check
`UsersByGroup` carried is gone; a table test runs every method with nil
options and with options set.

### The Link header parser reads rel only from the first parameter

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below, with no issue first.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3143](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3143)
  ("fix(client): skip a Link entry whose first parameter has no value",
  opened as "fix(client): find rel among all Link header parameters"), opened
  by this project's maintainer at 08:45 UTC on 2026-10-15. @heidi.berry asked GitLab
  Duo for a review at 19:29 UTC that day, which found nothing to comment on.
  Read on 2026-10-16 it is open and not approved. At 00:50 UTC on 2026-10-22
  @PatrickRice asked whether anything breaks on this today, wanting a test
  that fails without the fix. At 07:23 UTC we pushed `c17d316b`, which adds
  `TestPagination_Scan_KeysetBased_ParameterBeforeRel`: it runs
  `ListProjects` through `ScanAndCollect` over the two keyset pages of
  `TestPagination_Scan_KeysetBased`, with another parameter before `rel` in
  the first page's `Link` header, and on `main` at v3.30.1 it collects one
  page of two where the parameter has a value and panics in `Client.Do`
  where it has none. Our answer a minute later says that no GitLab header
  breaks it today, since every `Link` header GitLab writes carries `rel`
  alone, GitLab.com's through Cloudflare included, so the test is against a
  header something in between would write; we updated the description with
  it. Read at about 11:00 UTC that day it has no approval and that thread is
  open. At 23:43 UTC that day @PatrickRice asked @heidi.berry what she
  thinks: with little test coverage of the `Link` header he worries about
  breaking something for a case nobody reports, leans to "if it ain't broke
  don't fix it", and would wait for reports from users behind proxies first;
  at 23:45 UTC he added that he does not see how it would break anything and
  that the code makes sense, but that he defers to existing behaviour in the
  client's core files. Read at about 14:20 UTC on 2026-10-23 nobody has
  answered, and it has no approval. At 15:55 UTC that day we offered to
  narrow it to the panic alone; @PatrickRice accepted at 00:11 UTC on
  2026-10-24, to look at a fix like the first one if clients report proxies
  adding links, and at 08:20 UTC we force-pushed the branch as one commit,
  `d049e354`, under the new title. @heidi.berry approved it at 16:40 UTC that
  day, finding the current version fine, and @PatrickRice approved it at
  23:22 UTC on 2026-10-26 with "LGTM as well; on the merge train!".
- **Merged**: **partly, v3.38.1**. It merged at 23:43 UTC on 2026-10-26
  (squash commit `c57acd2a`) and is first in v3.38.1, tagged at 23:59 UTC
  that day: `populateLinkValues` skips an entry whose first parameter has no
  value, so `<url>; anchor; rel="next"` no longer panics, and still reads
  `rel` from the first parameter only, so that header and
  `<url>; type="application/json"; rel="next"` both leave `NextLink` empty.
  v3.40.0 reads it the same way. This server pins v3.30.0, where **What**
  still holds as written.
- **Blocking**: no. GitLab's own `Link` headers carry `rel` as their only
  parameter, so it takes something between this server and GitLab that adds
  or reorders parameters, a reverse proxy or a CDN. Behind one, a keyset list
  would publish no `next_page_token`: `keysetNextPageToken` in
  `internal/toolutil/pagination.go` reads `Response.NextLink`, which such a
  header leaves empty. A parameter with no value before `rel` makes the
  client-go call panic, which `recoverPanics` in `cmd/server/recover.go`
  answers as an internal error rather than losing the process. From v3.38.1
  such an entry is skipped instead, and the list ends after its first page.
- **Workaround**: none taken.

**Where**: `gitlab.go`, `Response.populateLinkValues`, which takes the
relation type of each `Link` entry from the first parameter after the URL,
as `strings.Split(parts[1], "=")[1]`
([gitlab.go line 1212](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/blob/95be8ccfe9d53662afa790a886a17ad1754ddd4d/gitlab.go#L1212)).

**What**: RFC 8288 lets link parameters come in any order and lets one have
no value. `<url>; anchor; rel="next"` makes `newResponse` panic with
`index out of range [1] with length 1`, and `Client.Do` calls `newResponse`
before it looks at the status code, so the panic escapes from whichever API
call received the response. `<url>; type="application/json"; rel="next"`
leaves `NextLink` empty, and since a keyset page carries no `X-Next-Page`,
the list ends after its first page without an error.

**How we found it**: reading how client-go fills `Response.NextLink`, which
this server reads to continue a keyset list since issue 1165.

**Fix merged**: the parser keeps reading `rel` from the first parameter and
skips an entry whose first parameter has no value.
`TestPaginationPopulateLinkValues` pins eleven headers, eight that parsed
before the fix, as they parse, and three that panicked, and
`TestClientDo_LinkParameterWithoutValue` lists a keyset page through
`ListProjects` with each of the two forms that panicked. Looking `rel` up by
name, ignoring case and the whitespace RFC 8288 allows, as the merge request
first proposed, waits on a report from a user behind a proxy.

### The wiki search decodes GitLab's blobs into wiki pages

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. v3.25.0, the head of main on 2026-10-15 (`26ff1abf`),
  carries the same signatures.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `search.wiki` hands the request a
  `gitlabclient.WithResponseCapture` context and decodes the captured body
  into `search.WikiBlobOutput`, which is the blob entity GitLab sends
  (ADR-0021), and ignores what client-go decoded. client-go reports no error
  for GitLab's answer, since no key of it is a key of `Wiki`; the handler also
  passes over the decode failure client-go would report for an answer holding
  a `Wiki` key with another type, which GitLab does not send, so that guard is
  defensive. It retires when the three methods return a type carrying the
  blob's fields.

**Where**: `search.go`, `WikiBlobs`, `WikiBlobsByGroup` and
`WikiBlobsByProject`, which decode `GET /search`, `GET /groups/:id/search` and
`GET /projects/:id/search` with `scope=wiki_blobs` into `[]*Wiki`, the wiki
page struct of `wikis.go` (`content`, `encoding`, `format`, `slug`, `title`).

**What**: GitLab answers the `wiki_blobs` scope with `API::Entities::Blob`
(`lib/api/search.rb`, `SCOPE_ENTITY`), the entity the `blobs` scope answers
with: `basename`, `data`, `path`, `filename`, `id`, `ref`, `startline`,
`project_id`, and `group_id` for a wiki result (`lib/api/entities/blob.rb`).
No key of it is a key of `Wiki`, so every result client-go returns is a struct
of empty strings, one per page found. The struct client-go returns for the
`blobs` scope, `Blob`, holds all of them but `group_id`.

**How we found it**: issue 1393. Publishing the blob id of a code search result
meant reading the entity each search scope presents, and the wiki scope
presents the same one; `search.wiki` published `slug`, `title`, `content` and
`format`, empty on every result, and the e2e scenario only logged the row
because it had nothing to assert.

**Effort**: small: a `WikiBlob` type (`Blob` plus `GroupID`) returned by the
three methods, a breaking change for callers, so it waits for a major version
or three parallel methods.

### SearchOptions models neither num_context_lines nor regex

- **Reported**: yes, as commit 39 of
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3063](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3063)
  (`be72781d` when pushed at 07:21 UTC, `8daec46a` after the merge request's
  force push of 13:44 UTC that day, `dcec96a5` since its rebase of
  2026-10-19), pushed on 2026-10-17.
- **In review**: yes, in that merge request, until it was closed unmerged on
  2026-10-21 ([entry 34](#response-structs-that-miss-a-field-gitlab-sends-unconditionally)
  says why); the commit goes out again in a small merge request on its
  topic, which this entry will name once it is opened.
- **Merged**: no. v3.25.0, the head of main on 2026-10-15, carries the same
  struct.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `search.code` takes `num_context_lines` and `regex` and
  adds each to the query client-go has encoded through a request option of
  its own (`codeSearchParams` in `internal/tools/search/search_params.go`),
  only when the caller set it, and refuses a `num_context_lines` outside 0 to
  20 before any request. It retires when the struct carries both fields with
  `omitempty`.

**Where**: `search.go`, `SearchOptions`, which every `SearchService` method
encodes into the query of `GET /search`, `GET /groups/:id/-/search` or
`GET /projects/:id/-/search`. At v3.15.0 it carries `ListOptions`, `Ref` and
`SearchType` and nothing else.

**What**: GitLab Enterprise declares both parameters on the three routes
(`ee/lib/ee/api/search.rb`), `regex` from 18.9 and `num_context_lines` from
18.11: `num_context_lines`, an integer from 0 to 20, the lines of context
advanced and exact code search put around each match (exact search only from
19.5), and `regex`, a boolean that tells exact code search whether the query
is a regular expression, which is how it reads the query when the parameter
is left out. Both are refused with 400 on a backend that does not take them,
on their presence rather than their value, so a struct carrying them has to
leave an unset one out of the query rather than send its zero. The backend is
the one that would answer, and a project search of a ref other than the
default branch is always answered by basic search
(`ee/app/services/ee/search/project_service.rb`), so either is refused there
whatever `search_type` says. A token carrying the `mcp` scope is never
refused: the check returns early for it, and the parameter is then ignored
where it does not apply. Community Edition, and Enterprise before the release
that declares a parameter, drop it.

**How we found it**: issue 1392. Exact code search over the API reads every
query as a regular expression unless `regex=false` is sent, so a caller
searching for literal text with a `.` or a `(` in it could not ask for it,
and could not widen the context around a match either.

**Effort**: small: two pointer fields with `url` tags and `omitempty`, and a
test that each reaches the query only when set.

  merged at 00:28 UTC on 2026-10-23, through @PatrickRice's merge train, in

  packages and `users`' own capture for the instance one,
  `CapturedSSHCertificate` and `CapturedSSHCertificates` for a group's SSH
  certificates, and `CapturedRunner` for a runner's details. Each is absent
  from an older instance's answer rather than published as off or empty. They
  retire when the structs carry the keys.

**What**: every key below is absent from the 19.4.1-ee live record and
present in the 19.5.0-ee one (`docs/development/gitlab-api-live.json`), and
client-go declares none of them.

- `Project` (`projects.go`) and `Group` (`groups.go`) declare no
  `duo_code_review_decisions_enabled`, which `ee/lib/ee/api/entities/project.rb`
  and `ee/lib/ee/api/entities/group.rb` expose while the
  `duo_code_review_decisions` feature flag is on and Duo code review is
  available, the group's to a caller who may administer it. projects.md calls
  it Ultimate only and dates it to 19.5, behind a flag that is off by default.
- `Group` declares no `require_sha_for_merge` or `lock_require_sha_for_merge`,
  which `lib/api/entities/group_detail.rb` exposes on every group read on its
  own: whether the group's merge requests need a valid commit SHA on the
  merge route, and whether that setting is enforced on every descendant group
  (groups.md).
- `GroupServiceAccount` (`group_serviceaccounts.go`), `ProjectServiceAccount`
  (`project_serviceaccounts.go`) and `ServiceAccount` (`users.go`) declare no
  `external`, which `lib/api/entities/service_account.rb` exposes on every
  account.
- `GroupSSHCertificate` (`group_ssh_certificates.go`) declares no
  `fingerprint`, which `lib/api/entities/ssh_certificate.rb` exposes on every
  certificate as the SHA256 fingerprint of the certificate authority's key,
  with its `SHA256:` prefix.
- `RunnerDetails` (`runners.go`) declares no `token_expires_at`, which
  `lib/api/entities/ci/runner_details.rb` exposes to a caller allowed to read
  the runner's sensitive data. `Runner` declares it, for the answer to a
  registration, and `RunnerDetails` does not embed `Runner`.
- `BasicUser` (`users.go`), which every merge request struct uses for its
  author, declares no `bot`, which `lib/api/entities/merge_request_author.rb`
  adds to `UserBasic` on every merge request author.

The parameters, each declared on its route in the 19.5.0-ee record and on no
client-go option struct:

- `UpdateGroupOptions` lacks `require_sha_for_merge`,
  `lock_require_sha_for_merge`, `duo_code_review_decisions_enabled` and
  `duo_auto_mode_availability` (`PUT /groups/:id`), and `CreateGroupOptions`
  the last (`POST /groups`).
- `CreateProjectOptions`, `CreateProjectForUserOptions` and
  `EditProjectOptions` lack `duo_code_review_decisions_enabled`. An import
  declares it under `override_params` as well and would not apply it even once
  client-go models it, since the import's tree restorer keeps only the project
  attributes `import_export.yml` permits and this is not one of them.
- `CreateServiceAccountUserOptions` and `UpdateServiceAccountOptions` lack
  `external` (`POST /service_accounts`, `PATCH /service_accounts/:user_id`).
- `SearchOptions` lacks the merge request filters the group and project search
  routes take: `author_username`, `label_name`, `source_branch`,
  `target_branch` and the `not[author_username]`, `not[source_branch]` and
  `not[target_branch]` negations.

**How we found it**: the sent dimension of the 1:1 audit
(`shapes.typed.unsurfaced` in `go run ./cmd/audit_1to1/ -scope=paths`),
which reported 41 undeclared findings as soon as the live record was
re-pinned to 19.5.0-ee
([issue 1023](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1023));
ten of them are the six keys above that are published where a type carries
the entity whole, and the other 31 are answered by declarations (the context
commit list's six keys, the commit types the same route reaches through
client-go, a share's confirmation, and two compact rows). The merge request
author's `bot` and the parameters came from a review of the diff between the
two records, which no gate reads.

**Effort**: small. Scalar members with `json` and `url` tags on eleven
structs, a pointer for each key an older instance leaves out.

### The rate limit backoff ignores Retry-After on a 429

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below, with no issue first.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3147](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3147)
  ("feat(client): add option to honor Retry-After when backing off from a
  429", opened as "fix(client): honor Retry-After when backing off from a
  429"), opened by this project's maintainer at 23:40 UTC on 2026-10-16 (one commit,
  `20b24175`) and readied for @PatrickRice at 23:43 UTC; its fork pipeline
  passed at 23:47 UTC. It is related to
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go#1311](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/issues/1311),
  closed, where the wait the client already takes from `Ratelimit-Reset`
  looked like a hang. @heidi.berry asked GitLab Duo for a review at 22:53
  UTC on 2026-10-17, which requested changes at 22:55 UTC with one finding:
  the guard against a value too large for a `time.Duration` covers only large
  positive values, so a large negative `Retry-After`, such as
  `-10000000000`, wraps to a wait of about 267 years, passes the `wait > 0`
  check and holds the request until its context ends, where the description
  promises the exponential fallback for a negative value. Read at 10:24 UTC
  on 2026-10-19 it is open on `20b24175` with no approval, that thread is
  unresolved, and nothing has been pushed since. At 14:45 UTC that day we
  pushed `d952a980`, in which `retryAfter` refuses a number of seconds that
  is not positive before multiplying it, and falls back to the exponential
  backoff for an HTTP date too far ahead for a `time.Duration`, which
  `time.Until` saturates and the jitter then wrapped to a negative wait;
  `TestRateLimitBackoff` gained three cases, and we answered the thread and
  resolved it. At 19:59 UTC we pushed `e4a25dca`, which makes the sum of the
  wait and its jitter saturate at the longest `time.Duration` instead of
  wrapping, for a `Ratelimit-Reset` far ahead as well, and updated the
  description. At 12:14 UTC on 2026-10-21 we asked @heidi.berry to request
  GitLab Duo's review again, since one requested from our account fails with
  `DCR4003` and the old review still requested changes; the contributor
  platform requested it at 18:47 UTC, and GitLab Duo found nothing and
  approved at 18:52 UTC. Read at about 11:00 UTC on 2026-10-22 it is open on
  `e4a25dca` with that approval alone, in milestone 19.6, its pipeline
  green, and no maintainer has reviewed it. At 11:57 UTC on 2026-10-26 we
  reminded @PatrickRice of it. At 15:36 UTC he asked how callers that fail
  fast on these 429s keep doing so, since the wait can now be ten minutes for
  the projects list limit or up to a day for project and group creation, and
  a deadline that ends during it hands the caller a context error instead of
  the 429; at 15:38 UTC he asked @heidi.berry. At 16:25 UTC we answered that
  the wait could give way to the exponential backoff when it would end after
  the request context's deadline, with no option, or that the whole change
  could be made opt-in. At 18:09 UTC @heidi.berry preferred it opt-in now and
  the default in a later major, 5.0, with a call-out in 4.0, and at 20:32 UTC
  @PatrickRice found our answer hard to read and asked for a concise one. At
  21:02 UTC we pushed `d8d23358`, which puts the wait behind a new client
  option, `WithRetryAfterBackoff()`, off by default, and keeps today's quick
  retries when the wait would end after the request context's deadline; the
  push reset GitLab Duo's approval, and its pipeline passed. We answered in
  three bullet points at 21:03 UTC, retitled it, and requested
  @PatrickRice's review again at 21:13 UTC. Read on 2026-10-31 it is open on
  `d8d23358`, in milestone 19.6, with that thread unresolved, no approval,
  and no review or comment since.
- **Merged**: no. v3.40.0, the newest tag on 2026-10-31, still reads
  `Ratelimit-Reset` alone.
- **Blocking**: no. This server never runs client-go's backoff:
  `retryOptions` in `internal/gitlab/retry.go` replaces it through
  `gl.WithCustomBackoff` with one that keeps the `RateLimit-Reset` reading,
  caps every wait at five seconds and retries twice (register row
  `RTC-006`), so the merge changes nothing here.
- **Workaround**: not needed. That backoff reads `RateLimit-Reset` alone as
  well, so a 429 carrying only `Retry-After` is retried after about 0.7 and
  1.4 seconds and then handed to the caller. Taking `Retry-After` there
  would still stop at the five-second ceiling, short of the minute most of
  these limits run for, and handing the 429 back rather than waiting past
  the ceiling is the choice that ceiling's comment sets out.

**Where**: `gitlab.go`, `rateLimitBackoff`, which on a 429 takes its wait
from `Ratelimit-Reset` alone and, without it, falls back to the exponential
backoff that starts at `RetryWaitMin`, 100 ms by default
([gitlab.go lines 848 to 869](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/blob/26ff1abf03ce5ce5433e396b14ff0bae8a2aacae/gitlab.go#L848-L869)
at v3.25.0, and the same function at v3.29.0).

**What**: since GitLab 18.5 the application rate limits the REST API checks
(`check_rate_limit!`, which hands the period of the limit to
`too_many_requests!`) answer a 429 with `Retry-After` and no
`RateLimit-Reset`: project and group export and import, note creation, tag
creation, search, listing projects and reading a user, among others. The
five default retries then wait less than five seconds in all, every one
lands inside the same window, and the caller gets the 429 back with its
retries spent. Rack::Attack throttles send both headers and are not
affected.

**How we found it**: reading client-go's 429 backoff, the one
`internal/gitlab/retry.go` replaces while keeping its intent. Nothing here
runs it, so no failure of this server led to it.

**Fix in review**: a client option, `WithRetryAfterBackoff()`, off by
default and the one exported name the change adds. With it,
`rateLimitBackoff` takes `Retry-After`, in seconds or as an HTTP date, as the
minimum wait when `Ratelimit-Reset` is absent, with the usual jitter on top,
unless that wait would end after the request context's deadline, where it
keeps the exponential backoff so the caller still gets the 429;
`Ratelimit-Reset` keeps its precedence. Its doc comment plans it as the
default in v5.0, with a call-out in v4.0. With or without the option, a wait
too close to the longest `time.Duration` for the jitter saturates rather
than wrapping. `TestRateLimitBackoff`,
`TestRateLimitBackoff_WithoutRetryAfterBackoff`, `TestRetryAfterWait`,
`TestWithRetryAfterBackoff` and three tests against an `httptest` server
cover it.

### UpdateSettingsOptions models twenty-six settings the update route does not take

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. All twenty-six are in the struct at v3.15.0 and still are
  at v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, and each of the 51 settings v3.16.0
  to v3.29.0 added is one the route declares; v3.30.0 adds none. Three carry
  a `Deprecated:` notice at v3.30.0: `housekeeping_bitmaps_enabled` ("Cannot
  be set through the API, always true"), which v3.15.0 carries already, and
  `autocomplete_users` and `autocomplete_users_unauthenticated` ("The API
  never accepted ..."), which v3.15.0 does not carry and v3.17.0 does, beside
  the `_limit` settings they point to. The other twenty-three carry none.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `admin.settings_update` refuses, by name and before
  anything is sent, a key client-go does not model, and since this pin it
  refuses these twenty-six the same way, in the same refusal
  (`unsendableSettingKeys` and `undeclaredSettingKeys` in
  `internal/tools/settings/settings.go`). Until then client-go modeled them,
  so the action sent them, and a patch naming one beside a setting the route
  takes was answered 200 with the rest applied and reported as applied
  whole, the half-applied patch the refusal exists to prevent. The list is
  written out, since the server does not carry the live record, and
  `TestUndeclaredSettingKeys_AreTheModeledKeysTheUpdateRouteDoesNotDeclare`
  holds it to the struct and the record, so a bump or a re-record that moves
  either fails until it follows. The refusal retires when client-go stops
  modeling them.

**Where**: `settings.go`, `UpdateSettingsOptions` (lines 596 to 1086 at
v3.29.0), which `UpdateSettings` sends to `PUT /application/settings`. Of
its 473 keys, 447 are among the 677 top-level params the 19.5.0 live record
declares on that route (`docs/development/gitlab-api-live.json`), and these
twenty-six are not declared there at all:

- `autocomplete_users` and `autocomplete_users_unauthenticated`;
- `ci_partitions_size_limit`;
- six `container_registry_import_*` settings: `created_before`,
  `max_retries`, `max_step_duration`, `max_tags_count`, `start_max_retries`
  and `target_plan`;
- `delayed_group_deletion` and `delayed_project_deletion`;
- `enforce_pat_expiration` and `enforce_ssh_key_expiration`;
- `help_text` and `sign_in_text`;
- `housekeeping_bitmaps_enabled`, `in_product_marketing_emails_enabled`,
  `pseudonymizer_enabled`, `repository_storages`,
  `send_user_confirmation_email` and `suggest_pipeline_enabled`;
- three `throttle_unauthenticated_git_lfs_*` settings: `enabled`,
  `period_in_seconds` and `requests_per_period`;
- `user_email_lookup_limit` and `web_ide_clientside_preview_enabled`.

**What**: the route builds the update from
`declared_params(include_missing: false)`
([lib/api/settings.rb:661](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/settings.rb#L661)
at `v19.5.0-ee`), so Grape drops every key it does not declare, and it
declares none of these. Part of its params come from
`Helpers::SettingsHelpers.optional_attributes` when the application loads,
which is why the live record, read from a booted GitLab, is the list to
compare with and the source is not. A key among them is dropped without a
word: a patch that names it beside a setting the route takes is answered
200, the other setting applied and this one not, and one that names nothing
else is answered 400, since the route requires at least one of the settings its
`at_least_one_of` lists. Seven of them GitLab still sends on a read, each with a fixed value:
the six `container_registry_import_*` settings as `0` or `""`, which the
entity keeps "to be backwards compatible", and `housekeeping_bitmaps_enabled`
as `true`
([lib/api/entities/application_setting.rb:55-82](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/entities/application_setting.rb#L55-82)),
so a caller reads them on every answer and cannot change them. GitLab's own
API page still lists one of them as a setting a caller can change:
`ci_partitions_size_limit` is in the available settings of
`doc/api/settings.md` at `v19.5.0-ee`, while GitLab removed the setting in
18.11.0
([gitlab-org/gitlab!227211](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/227211)).

**How we found it**: recounting, for the move of the pin to v3.29.0, how
many of the route's params the struct models, a figure the settings
handler's comment and tests state. Read the other way round, the struct's
473 keys left twenty-six that the route does not declare.

**Effort**: small: a `Deprecated:` notice on each of the twenty-three that
carry none, saying the API drops it, and the fields' removal at the next
major version.

### ListTopicsOptions and CreateTopicOptions model no organization_id

- **Reported**: yes, by another contributor:
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go#2313](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/work_items/2313)
  ("Add missing organization_id option to ListTopics and CreateTopic"),
  opened on 2026-10-10, open.
- **In review**: yes, theirs:
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3105](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3105)
  ("feat(topics): add organization_id to ListTopics and CreateTopic
  options"), opened on 2026-10-10 and closing that issue, adds
  `OrganizationID *int64` to both structs, the create's marked experimental
  at a client-go maintainer's request of 2026-10-14, which the author applied
  on 2026-10-15. Read on 2026-10-31 it is open, in milestone 19.6, and still
  shows the review's requested changes. None by us, since the change is
  already in review.
- **Merged**: no. At v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, `ListTopicsOptions`
  carries the page, `search` and `without_projects` (added in v3.16.0), and
  `CreateTopicOptions` carries `name`, `title`, `description` and the avatar.
  `Topic` already decodes `organization_id`, one of the gaps of
  [entry 34](#response-structs-that-miss-a-field-gitlab-sends-unconditionally)
  that merged. v3.40.0 carries neither field either.
- **Blocking**: no. Without the parameter GitLab lists and creates topics in
  the organization it resolves for the request, which on an instance with
  only the default organization is the only one there is.
- **Workaround**: none. `admin.topic_list` and `admin.topic_create` do not
  offer `organization_id`, so each acts on the organization GitLab resolves
  for the request. [Issue 1236](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1236),
  closed on 2026-10-20, recorded offering it on the list once a client-go
  release carries it; this row now holds that wait.

**Where**: `topics.go`, `ListTopicsOptions` (line 93 at v3.29.0), which
`ListTopics` sends to `GET /topics`, and `CreateTopicOptions`, which
`CreateTopic` sends to `POST /topics`.

**What**: both routes declare `organization_id`, an integer that defaults to
the request's current organization
([lib/api/topics.rb:29-30](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/topics.rb#L29-30)
for the list and
[lines 71 and 72](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/topics.rb#L71-72)
for the create, at `v19.5.0-ee`), and the 19.5.0 live record holds both. The
list hands the organization it finds to `Projects::TopicsFinder`, which
returns that organization's topics and no others
(`Projects::Topic.in_organization`, `app/finders/projects/topics_finder.rb`
line 16), and the create saves the topic in the organization the param
names. A caller of client-go therefore reads and creates topics only in the
organization GitLab resolves for it and cannot name another, while every
topic it reads carries its `organization_id`.

**How we found it**: issue 1236, from the 403 hint of `admin.topic_list`,
which named `without_projects` while the action did not take it. The live
record declares `organization_id` beside it on `GET /topics`, and client-go
v3.16.0 added the one and not the other. The create half was found while
writing this entry.

**Effort**: small: an `OrganizationID *int64` with `url` and `json` tags and
`omitempty` on both structs, and a test that each reaches the request only
when set.

### ListPipelineTriggerJobsOptions models no include_retried, which the trigger job routes read and do not declare

- **Reported**: no, on either side.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. `ListPipelineTriggerJobsOptions`, which v3.24.0 added with
  `ListPipelineTriggerJobs` through another contributor's
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3134](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3134),
  carries the page and `scope` and nothing else at v3.30.0, the version
  `go.mod` pins, while the `ListJobsOptions` the deprecated
  `ListPipelineBridges` takes carries `include_retried`. GitLab 19.5.0
  declares the parameter on neither trigger job route.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. On an instance on 19.2 or later `job.list_bridges`
  lists through `trigger_jobs` and adds `include_retried=true` to the query
  client-go encoded through a request option of its own (`includeRetried` in
  `internal/tools/jobs/jobs.go`), only when the caller asked;
  `TestListBridges_NineteenTwoOrLater_ListsThroughTriggerJobs` holds it. On
  an older instance it lists through `bridges`, where `ListJobsOptions`
  carries the field, and sets it only when the caller asked, never to
  `false`. The request option retires when the struct carries the field.

**Where**: `jobs.go`, `ListPipelineTriggerJobsOptions` (line 347 at
v3.29.0), which `ListPipelineTriggerJobs` sends to
`GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/trigger_jobs`; and on GitLab's
side the declarations of that route and of
`GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/bridges` in
`lib/api/ci/pipelines.rb`.

**What**: at `v19.5.0-ee` both routes declare `pipeline_id`, `scope` and the
page and nothing else
([lib/api/ci/pipelines.rb:231-235](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/ci/pipelines.rb#L231-235)
and
[257-261](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/ci/pipelines.rb#L257-261)),
and the 19.5.0 live record agrees, while the pipeline jobs route above them
declares `include_retried` as a Boolean that defaults to false (line 191).
Both trigger job routes run `present_pipeline_trigger_jobs`
([lines 471 to 482](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/lib/api/ci/pipelines.rb#L471-482)),
which hands Grape's `params` whole, not its declared params, to
`Ci::JobsFinder`, and `pipeline_jobs` there keeps a pipeline's retried jobs
when `params[:include_retried]` is set and only its latest ones otherwise
([app/finders/ci/jobs_finder.rb:66-72](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/app/finders/ci/jobs_finder.rb#L66-72)).
So GitLab honours a parameter the routes do not declare, and its page for
them (`doc/api/jobs.md`, "List all trigger jobs by pipeline") does not name
it. Being undeclared, it is not coerced either: the finder reads the string
it arrived as, which Ruby holds true whatever it says, so, read from the
source and not measured, `include_retried=false` returns the retried jobs as
`true` does. client-go's `ListJobsOptions.IncludeRetried` is a `*bool`, so a
caller of `ListPipelineBridges` who sets it to `false` sends exactly that,
and a caller of `ListPipelineTriggerJobs` cannot ask for retried trigger
jobs at all.

**How we found it**: moving `job.list_bridges` onto `trigger_jobs` with the
v3.29.0 pin. The new options had no field for the `include_retried` the
action already offered, and reading why the old route honoured it showed
that neither route declares it.

**Effort**: small on each side. In client-go, an `IncludeRetried *bool`
with `url` and `json` tags and `omitempty` on
`ListPipelineTriggerJobsOptions`, and a test that it reaches the query. In
GitLab, `optional :include_retried, type: Boolean, default: false` on both
routes, as the pipeline jobs route declares it, which also makes `false`
mean false, and the parameter in the page's table.

### BranchAccessDescription and GroupBranchAccessDescription model no member_role_name

- **Reported**: no, not yet. It goes out as a small merge request of its
  own, at the pace of the small merge requests that replace the joint one
  [entry 34](#response-structs-that-miss-a-field-gitlab-sends-unconditionally)
  describes.
- **In review**: no, not yet.
- **Merged**: no. v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, added `member_role_id`
  to both structs and to the two permission option structs through another
  contributor's
  [gitlab-org/api/client-go!3149](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3149),
  and not the name GitLab sends beside it.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. Every handler that answers with a protected branch
  rule reads `member_role_name` off the captured response beside the SDK's
  decode
  ([ADR-0021](adr/adr-0021-captured-response-for-fields-the-sdk-does-not-model.md)),
  one `toolutil.ProtectedRefAccessExtra` per access level in GitLab's order:
  `Protect` (its 409 path included), `ProtectedGet`, `ProtectedList` and
  `ProtectedUpdate` in `internal/tools/branches`, behind `branch.protect`,
  `branch.get_protected`, `branch.list_protected` and
  `branch.update_protected`, through `toolutil.CapturedProtectedBranch` and
  `CapturedProtectedBranches`; and `List`, `Get`, `Protect` and `Update` in
  `internal/tools/groupprotectedbranches`, behind
  `group.protected_branch_list`, `group.protected_branch_get`,
  `group.protected_branch_protect` and `group.protected_branch_update`,
  through `toolutil.CapturedGroupProtectedBranch` and
  `CapturedGroupProtectedBranches`. A name that does not decode as a string
  fails the call rather than reaching the caller as an empty one
  (`TestProtectedBranches_UnreadableCapturedMemberRoleName` and
  `TestGroupProtectedBranches_UnreadableCapturedMemberRoleName`). The
  `audit_project_full` prompt, the one that renders branch protection, reads
  it the same way, through `CapturedProtectedBranches` in
  `handleAuditProjectFull` (`internal/prompts/prompt_audit.go`), names a
  custom role as the tools do, and reports the section unread when a name
  does not decode
  (`TestAuditProjectFull_UnreadableCapturedMemberRoleName_LeavesTheSectionUnread`).
  The capture retires when both structs carry the field.

**Where**: `protected_branches.go`, `BranchAccessDescription`, and
`group_protected_branches.go`, `GroupBranchAccessDescription`, which decode
each entry of a protected branch's `push_access_levels`,
`merge_access_levels` and `unprotect_access_levels` on every project and
group protected branch route that answers with a rule.

**What**: `ee/lib/ee/api/entities/protected_ref_access.rb` exposes
`member_role_id` and `member_role_name` together, under one condition: the
access level can carry a member role and custom roles are licensed for its
namespace, which is Ultimate. `member_role_name` is the name of the custom
role the level grants, read through the level's `member_role`, and null on a
level that grants none. `Entities::ProtectedBranch` and `Entities::GroupProtectedBranch`
both present their three arrays through that entity, and the 19.5.0 live
record (`docs/development/gitlab-api-live.json`) holds both keys on
`API::Entities::ProtectedRefAccess` under that condition. client-go v3.30.0
decodes the id and drops the name, so a caller of the SDK learns which
custom role a rule grants only by its number.

**How we found it**: moving the pin to v3.30.0, which added `member_role_id`
to both structs. The entity in the live record exposes the name beside it,
and R-PATH's sent report had not named it, since it judges a type against
the entity its routes annotate and not the entity a nested array renders
with.

**Effort**: small: a `MemberRoleName string` with its `json` tag on both
structs, and a test that each decodes it.

### The protected environment approval rule options model an access_level_description no route declares

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. All four option structs carry the field at v3.30.0, the
  version `go.mod` pins.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. The two approval rule inputs
  `internal/tools/protectedenvs` and `internal/tools/groupprotectedenvs`
  both send, `ApprovalRuleInput` and `UpdateApprovalRuleInput`, which
  `internal/tools/protectedenvdata` declares once for the four option
  structs, no longer offer `access_level_description`, so
  `environment.protected_protect`, `environment.protected_update`,
  `group.protected_env_protect` and `group.protected_env_update` never
  send it, and the individual tools' item schemas, which are closed,
  refuse a call that names it
  (`TestApprovalRuleInputs_OfferNoAccessLevelDescription`, and a case of
  `TestProtectedEnvironmentSchemas_IndividualTool_HoldsEachEntry` and of
  `TestGroupProtectedEnvSchemas_IndividualTool_HoldsEachEntry`). Until then
  the inputs offered it as "Human-readable description of the access level"
  and the handlers sent it, and a caller who set it changed nothing. Nothing
  retires: the inputs stay without it whether or not client-go drops it,
  since GitLab does not take it.

**Where**: `protected_environments.go`, `EnvironmentApprovalRuleOptions`
(line 156 at v3.30.0) and `UpdateEnvironmentApprovalRuleOptions` (line 211),
and `group_protected_environments.go`, `GroupEnvironmentApprovalRuleOptions`
(line 156) and `UpdateGroupEnvironmentApprovalRuleOptions` (line 210), the
`approval_rules` entries of `ProtectRepositoryEnvironments`,
`UpdateProtectedEnvironments`, `ProtectGroupEnvironment` and
`UpdateGroupProtectedEnvironment`.

**What**: the approval rule block of
[ee/lib/api/protected_environments.rb](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.5.0-ee/ee/lib/api/protected_environments.rb)
declares `user_id`, `group_id`, `group_inheritance_type`, `id`, `_destroy`,
`access_level` and `required_approvals`, and nothing else, for the project
and the group routes alike, and the 19.5.0 live record
(`docs/development/gitlab-api-live.json`) holds those seven
`approval_rules[...]` params on all four routes and no
`approval_rules[access_level_description]`. The routes build the rules from
`declared_params(include_missing: false)`, so Grape drops the key.
`access_level_description` is a field GitLab computes and answers with, the
rule's `humanize` in `ee/app/models/protected_environments/authorizable.rb`,
which the response structs rightly decode; the four option structs carry it
as if a caller could set it.

**How we found it**: issue 1271, while stating GitLab's rules about an
approval rule entry in the item schemas of the four actions: the item schema
offered a property no route declares.

**Effort**: small: the field removed from the four option structs, a
breaking change of the module's API, or marked `Deprecated:` with the reason
until the next major.

### Five response structs miss keys this server reads through a raw request instead

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. None of the keys below is modeled at v3.30.0, the version
  `go.mod` pins, or at v3.38.0.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. Each read below sends its own request through
  client-go's `NewRequest` and decodes the answer into a struct of the
  handler's own, the client-go struct embedded or copied, so the request
  keeps client-go's base URL, retries and context. Each is an entry of the
  upstream wait table (`cmd/audit_1to1/internal/waits`), with a `LacksKey`
  predicate per key, so the `sdk` scope of `cmd/audit_1to1` says which read
  can go back to its client-go method the day a pin models the keys.

**Where** and **What**:

- `Deployment` (`deployments.go`) models none of `approvals`,
  `approval_summary` and `pending_approval_count`, and its
  `DeploymentDeployable` has no `project`. `environment.deployment_get` and
  `environment.deployment_list` decode into `deploymentAPI`
  (`internal/tools/deployments`, `rawGetDeployment` and
  `rawListDeployments`), in place of `GetProjectDeployment` and
  `ListProjectDeployments`.
- `Job` (`jobs.go`) models neither `archived` nor `runner_manager`, its
  `JobRunner` none of `ip_address`, `paused`, `runner_type`, `online` and
  `status`, and it types `duration`, `queued_duration` and `coverage`
  `float64`, which reads a null as 0 (row 116). The job lists and reads
  decode into `jobAPI` (`internal/tools/jobs`, `rawListJobs` and
  `rawGetJob`), with the runner as a struct of its own and the three
  measures as pointers, in place of `ListProjectJobs`.
- `MergeRequestApprovalRule` (`merge_request_approvals.go`) has no
  `overridden`, which each rule of the list, the create, the update and the
  approval state carries. `internal/tools/mrapprovals` decodes all four into
  a rule of its own, in place of `GetApprovalRules`, `CreateApprovalRule`,
  `UpdateApprovalRule` and `GetApprovalState`.
- `GPGSignature` (`commits.go`) models the PGP signature alone: no
  `signature_type`, no `commit_source`, no `key` for an SSH signature and no
  `x509_certificate`. The commit signature read decodes into
  `gpgSignatureAPI` (`internal/tools/commits`, `rawGetGPGSignature`), in
  place of `GetGPGSignature`.
- `GroupEpicBoard` (`group_epic_boards.go`) models neither
  `hide_backlog_list` nor `hide_closed_list`, and the elements of its two
  lists fall short too: its `labels` are `LabelDetails` (`issues.go`), with
  none of `title`, `group_id`, `project_id`, `template`, `created_at` and
  `updated_at`, and its `lists` are `BoardList` (`boards.go`), with neither
  `list_type` nor `collapsed`. `internal/tools/groupepicboards` reads both
  epic board routes through `rawListBoards` and `rawGetBoard`, so no handler
  calls `GroupEpicBoards`.

**How we found it**: the upstream wait table. Every raw request of the tool
packages has to name the register row it waits on, and these five had none:
they were written before the register asked a workaround for its row. Each
key above is one the struct a read decodes into carries beside client-go's,
which the table's `sdk` scope holds to a predicate one by one.

**Effort**: small: the keys added to the five structs and to the
`JobRunner`, `LabelDetails` and `BoardList` they hold, and the three
measures made pointers, each with its response test.

### Routes this server or its e2e suite sends have no client-go method, or one that takes no options

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no, at v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, or at v3.38.0.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes, a request of our own or a request option for each,
  each an entry of the upstream wait table (`cmd/audit_1to1/internal/waits`)
  with a `NoMethodFor` or `TakesNoOptions` predicate.

**Where** and **What**:

- `POST /orbit/mcp`, GitLab's Orbit MCP endpoint, which `orbit.tools`,
  `orbit.dsl` and the llm text of `orbit.schema` read since GitLab.com
  removed `GET /orbit/tools`, `GET /orbit/schema/dsl` and `GET /orbit/schema`,
  the routes `Orbit.GetTools`, `Orbit.GetDsl` and `Orbit.GetSchema` send
  (rows 145 to 147). No method sends it, so `orbit.callMCP` builds the POST
  through `NewRequest`.
- `GET /groups/:id/hooks/:hook_id/events`, the deliveries of a group hook.
  client-go has `ResendGroupHookEvent` for one delivery and nothing that
  lists them, so the e2e fixture reads them through `NewRequest`
  (`test/e2e/internal/fixture`, `listGroupHookEvents`).
- `PUT /projects/:id/packages/ml_models/:model_version_id/files/(*path/):file_name`,
  the upload of a file into a model version's package. `ModelRegistry` has
  the download and nothing that uploads, so the model registry scenario puts
  the file through `NewRequest` (`test/e2e/gitlab/common`, `uploadModelFile`).
- `ListProjectMarkdownUploads` takes no options struct, so the upload list
  writes its paging and ordering into the query through a request option
  (`internal/tools/uploads`, `listQueryParameters`).
- `ListGroupSSHCertificates` takes no options struct, so the certificate list
  writes its paging into the query the same way
  (`internal/tools/groupsshcerts`, `listQueryParameters`).
- Sixteen more methods of a paginated list take no options struct either:
  `Attestations.ListAttestations`, `Commits.ListMergeRequestsByCommit`,
  `Issues.GetParticipants`,
  `MergeRequestContextCommits.ListMergeRequestContextCommits`, the four
  `MergeRequests` lists `GetMergeRequestDependencies`,
  `GetMergeRequestParticipants`, `GetMergeRequestReviewers` and
  `ListMergeRequestPipelines`, `PagesDomains.ListAllPagesDomains`,
  `ProjectAliases.ListProjectAliases`, the two `ResourceGroup` lists
  `GetAllResourceGroupsForAProject` and
  `ListUpcomingJobsForASpecificResourceGroup`, `SystemHooks.ListHooks`, and
  `Users.ListEmails`, `Users.ListGPGKeys` and `Users.ListGPGKeysForUser`.
  Without options a method can only ever ask for GitLab's first page, so
  every action that lists through one writes `page` and `per_page` into the
  query through `toolutil.PaginationRequestOption`.

**How we found it**: the upstream wait table, for the reason the previous
entry gives. The sixteen were declared a raw reason of their own until a
review of the table asked why a method that takes no options waits on
nothing upstream, when the upload and certificate lists, the same gap, did.

**Effort**: small to medium: two methods, and an options struct, or a
`ListOptions` parameter, for each of the eighteen lists.

### `UploadRequest` writes only the first value of each field

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no, at v3.30.0, the version `go.mod` pins, or at v3.38.0.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes, in the two creates that send a list beside an
  avatar. The upstream wait table cannot hold it, since its predicates read
  types and routes and this is the body of a function, so
  `TestSDK_CreateProjectWithAvatar_WritesTheFirstTopicAlone`
  (`internal/tools/projects`) pins what client-go sends instead and fails
  the day it sends more.

**Where**: `gitlab.go`, `(*Client).UploadRequest` (line 1106 at v3.30.0,
1108 at v3.38.0). It writes the options of an upload as multipart fields
from go-querystring's `query.Values`, one `w.WriteField(name,
fields.Get(name))` per name, and `url.Values.Get` is the first value. A
list option therefore reaches GitLab as its first element alone, and only
on the request that carries a file: the same options in a JSON body go out
whole. Every method that switches to an upload when its options carry an
avatar does it (`CreateProject`, `CreateProjectForUser`, `EditProject`,
`CreateGroup`, `UpdateGroup`, `CreateTopic`, `UpdateTopic`, `CreateUser`
and `ModifyUser`), and so does the project import. client-go knows the
shape of it in one place: `CreateGroup` refuses an avatar beside more than
one access level of the default branch protection, "as it will result in
unexpected behavior".

**What** this server does about it, in the handlers that send a list
beside an avatar:

- `projects.attachAvatar` sends the topics and the tags as one
  comma-separated value (`commaJoined`), which GitLab splits back
  (`API::Validations::Types::CommaSeparatedToArray`).
- `groups.attachAvatar` sends `unique_project_download_limit_allowlist`
  the same way, which `ee/lib/ee/api/helpers/groups_helpers.rb` splits
  back.
- `groups.Create` refuses `unique_project_download_limit_alertlist` beside
  an avatar before any request, since it is an `Array[Integer]` GitLab does
  not split, and points at `group.update`.

Writing every value would not be the whole fix: Rack keeps the last value
of a field sent twice under one name, and builds a list only from a name
that ends in `[]`. So when the pin fails, each of the three sites is looked
at again rather than removed.

**How we found it**: offering the avatar R-PARAM listed as not offered on
the project and group creates. The group create's test sent two usernames
in the allowlist beside an avatar, and the mock read one.

**Effort**: small: one part per value in `UploadRequest`, under a name a
list can be read back from, and a test.
