  `CustomEmoji` line, and every other line, no.
- **Blocking**: yes, for a fine-grained personal access token, whatever its
  grant: at 19.5.0, 36 actions cannot be served it and 8 are served with
  parts of their answer empty. A classic token is unaffected. The 36 are
  this entry's share of phase A, the 55 of 1098 actions no fine-grained token
  reaches at 19.5.0, every one of them through GraphQL, as `make
  audit-1to1-grants-report` counts them on 2026-10-17: 33 behind an
  undeclared type and 3 behind an undeclared mutation, all in the table
  below, and 19 writes whose payload type declares nothing, which are
  [row 88](#a-declared-mutation-whose-payload-type-declares-nothing-commits-the-write-and-answers-null)'s.
- **Workaround**: yes. The 36 are withheld from every fine-grained session
  with the reason, the GitLab release the verdict comes from and the way out,
  a classic token (register row `AUT-007`), so a model is never handed an
  empty answer that reads as "nothing there"; the 8 are served with a note
  naming each part GitLab leaves empty. `cmd/gen_action_grants` derives both
  sets from the handlers and the live record, and `make audit-1to1-grants-report`
  prints this list as the worklist of this entry's contributions, each element
  with the REST routes that already declare a permission for the same
  resource. Serving over REST what GraphQL cannot serve such a token is
  [issue 1054](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1054).
  Each declaration GitLab adds retires its line, once the live record is taken
  from the release that carries it (Adopting a declaration, below).

**Where**: GitLab's GraphQL authorization of a fine-grained token
(`lib/gitlab/graphql/authz/granular_scope_authorization.rb` at `v19.4.1-ee`):
an enforced object type or a mutation whose class carries no
`authorize_granular_token` directive denies every fine-grained token
(`return error(default_error_message) if token.granular?`), and a denied
object is answered `null`, or left out of a connection, with no error
(`app/graphql/types/base_object.rb`; the schema keeps graphql-ruby's
`unauthorized_object`).

**What**: the undeclared types and mutations on a path this server's
documents reach, as `go run ./cmd/audit_1to1/ -scope=grants` reports them at
19.5.0 (at 19.4.1 the second line named `CustomEmoji` too, withholding
`custom_emoji.list`):

| Type or mutation                                                                            | What a fine-grained token gets                    | Actions                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Namespace`                                                                                 | `null` for every root `namespace(fullPath:)` read | 24: 14 epic actions, the work item reads and writes and the saved view reads, `achievement.list` and two more  |
| `UserAchievement`, `BranchRule`, `ProjectTargetBranchRule`, `PipelineSecurityReportFinding` | The items removed from the list                   | `achievement.user_list`, `branch.rule_list`, `project.target_branch_rule_list`, `security_finding.list`        |
| `CiCatalogResource`, `SecurityReportSummary`, `VulnerabilitySeveritiesCount`                | `null`                                            | `ci_catalog.get`, `ci_catalog.list`, `vulnerability.pipeline_security_summary`, `vulnerability.severity_count` |
| `ScanProfileProjectStatus`                                                                  | A list of non-null items answered `null` whole    | `security_scan_profile.list_project_statuses`                                                                  |
| `bulkUpdateSecurityAttributes`, `securityScanProfileAttach`, `securityScanProfileDetach`    | Refused, nothing runs                             | `security_attribute.bulk_update`, `security_scan_profile.attach`, `security_scan_profile.detach`               |
| `VulnerabilityIssueLink`, `VulnerabilityFindingTokenStatus`, `VulnerableKubernetesResource` | Those fields empty, the rest served               | `vulnerability.get`, `vulnerability.list` and the four state mutations                                         |
| `QuickActionsStatus`                                                                        | That payload field empty, the note served         | `group.epic_note_update`, `group.epic_discussion_update_note`                                                  |

The probes of `test/e2e/gitlab` measured the shapes on a 19.4.1 instance: a
`namespace(fullPath:)` read answers `null`, a project's `branchRules` loses
its items and `vulnerabilitySeveritiesCount` answers `null`, each with no
error, where a classic token reads them
(`TestFineGrainedProbes_UndeclaredGraphQLTypes_AreEmptyWithNoError`,
`TestFineGrainedProbes_SeverityCount_IsNullWithNoError`). For four of the
types a REST route of the same resource does declare a permission (the
protected branches routes for `BranchRule`, the namespace routes for
`Namespace`, the issue links routes for `VulnerabilityIssueLink`, the epic
routes for `WorkItem` in row 89), which is where the declaration GitLab would
add can start from.

**A related blind spot**, read on 2026-10-05:
[gitlab-org/gitlab#627165](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/627165)
(`group::authorization`, opened 2026-09-01, assigned to this project's
maintainer since 2026-10-28) records that a mutation
which calls `Authz::Tokens::AuthorizeGranularScopesService` in its resolver,
because the boundary it needs is not a top-level argument, is invisible to
GitLab's documentation generator, to `gitlab:permissions:validate` and to its
spec scanner, all of which read only the directives. `cmd/gen_api_live` reads
the same directives, so a requirement checked that way is invisible to
R-GRANT as well, and the derivation would understate what such an action
needs. No action of this server reaches the issue's three examples
(`promoteToEpic`, `epicTreeReorder` and `projectSubscriptionCreate`) today.
On 2026-10-30 @alexbuijs confirmed on the issue that no GraphQL resolver on
`master` calls the service any more, and ours,
[gitlab-org/gitlab!266660](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/266660)
("Add a cop that flags manual granular token checks in GraphQL",
`Gitlab/Authz/UseGranularTokenDirective`), merged at 14:32 UTC that day in
milestone 19.6, keeps it that way; the issue it closes is still open.

**How we found it**: the fine-grained derivation of issue 952, which walks
every GraphQL document an action sends against the authorization a booted
19.4.1 records (`cmd/gen_api_live`), and the direct probes above.

**Proposal**: declare `authorize_granular_token` on each, starting with
`Namespace`, which alone withholds 24 actions, at the boundary and with the
permission the matching REST route already declares where one exists.

**What this asks of GitLab**, element by element, as
[issue 1055](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1055) set it
out before this entry replaced it on 2026-10-07. For each type or mutation of
the table: first establish what GitLab intends, whether an issue or epic of
its fine-grained token rollout already covers it (the W1.2 issue named under
Reported covers part), whether a merge request is in flight, or whether it is
left undeclared on purpose (a `skip_reason`, or a statement in the tracking
issue). Where it is pending and nobody has it, prepare a GitLab merge request
that declares it with the assignable permission and boundary GitLab already
uses for the equivalent REST route, removes its line from
`config/authz/graphql/authorization_todo.txt` (issue 1055 placed it under
`lib/tasks/gitlab/permissions/graphql/`, which is wrong), carries request
specs under `spec/requests/api/graphql` or
`ee/spec/requests/api/graphql` with GitLab's shared examples ("authorizing
granular token permissions for GraphQL") and an N+1 guard for a list
position, and passes `gitlab:permissions:graphql:compile_docs` and
`gitlab:permissions:validate`. Then record each one here with the release
that carries its declaration, so the withheld set shrinks by recorded release
and never by assumption. Nothing is posted to gitlab.com, merge request,
issue or comment, before the maintainer has reviewed the list of what is
proposed.

**One blocker for `Namespace`**: its assignable permission, `read_namespace`
(`config/authz/permission_groups/assignable_permissions/groups/namespace/read.yml`),
allows the `user` and `project` boundaries only, at `v19.4.1-ee` and on
`master` read on 2026-10-07, so a declaration at the group boundary, which
the W1.2 issue asks for beside the project one, needs that assignable amended
in the same change. `gitlab-org/gitlab!261599` amended it as merged on
2026-10-29: the assignable now allows the `group`, `project` and `user`
boundaries, so the blocker goes with the release that carries the merge,
19.6 at the earliest.

**Adopting a declaration**: once a release carries it, the live record is
taken from that release (`make gen-api-live`) and the grants table derived
again (`make gen-action-grants`), which drops the element from the withheld
set with no code of its own. Two end-to-end probes pin today's `null` and flip
for their elements,
`TestFineGrainedProbes_UndeclaredGraphQLTypes_AreEmptyWithNoError` and
`TestFineGrainedProbes_SeverityCount_IsNullWithNoError`, and the
`group-work-item` declarations of `cmd/gen_action_grants/grant_declarations.go`
went with row 89 when the record was taken from 19.5.0. The cost is ADR-0024's NEG-001: the withheld set is the newest
record's, so an instance older than the release that carries a declaration is
served an action it answers with a silent `null`. Re-pinning the record at
each minor is
[issue 1023](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1023), and
how GitLab could fail visibly instead is the merge request
[issue 1103](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1103)
prepared, described under
[row 88](#a-declared-mutation-whose-payload-type-declares-nothing-commits-the-write-and-answers-null).
Until then, when such an instance answers one of the writes of row 88 or the
epic creation of row 89 without its object, the handler reports it to a
fine-grained session as probably committed rather than as not done.

**The two other findings issue 1055 carried.** The self route omitting a
token's granular scopes is
[row 86](#a-tokens-own-description-omits-its-granular-scopes), whose fix merged
on 2026-10-07. The other was that `validate_unique_namespace` in
`app/services/authz/granular_scope_service.rb` appeared to accept two scopes
with the same namespace in one creation request, recorded only from the `201`
of that creation and so to be measured again before it was reported. GitLab
is fixing it itself:
[gitlab-org/gitlab!259531](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/259531)
("Reject duplicate granular scopes within one request", `group::authorization`,
milestone 19.5, opened 2026-10-05, open on 2026-10-07) describes the same gap,
incoming scopes never compared with each other, and calls the result
redundant rows rather than a security hole. Read on 2026-10-08 it is still
open, approved by @alexbuijs at 09:19 UTC on 2026-10-07 and waiting on its
database review. @daniele-gitlab approved it for authentication at 13:12 UTC
on 2026-10-09 with one non-blocking suggestion, and at 08:25 UTC on
2026-10-10 the release tooling moved it to milestone 19.6 with
`missed:19.5`; read that day it is still open and waiting on the database
review. @eugielimpin set it to join the merge train at 01:38 UTC on
2026-10-12, and it merged at 02:53 UTC (merge commit `09e28981`), in
milestone 19.6, and reached GitLab.com's production stage at 10:22 UTC.
Its milestone notwithstanding, it merged before the 19.5 cut and is in
`v19.5.0-ee`, read on 2026-10-16. It
costs this server nothing and
leaves nothing for us to do, so it has no row of its own.

### A declared mutation whose payload type declares nothing commits the write and answers null

- **Reported**: no. The merge request that proposes a visible error for a
  fine-grained denial, this one among them, is written (issue 1103, below
  under **Proposal**), and the maintainer decided on 2026-10-10 to open it
  after a second review of its text.
- **In review**: yes, partly. Ours, for two of the payload types below:
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!266080](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/266080)
  ("Authorize fine-grained tokens to read achievements"), opened from the
  community fork on 2026-10-29, adds the assignable permission
  `read_achievement` at the group and user boundaries, declares the user
  boundary on `UserAchievement` and `UserAchievementCount` and the group
  boundary on `Namespace.achievements`, and lets `Achievement` skip with
  `parent_authorizes`; read on 2026-10-31 it is open, approved by @idurham
  with four approvals left, after @alexbuijs chose that day to keep its
  design over the split @jayswain proposed. GitLab's own, for two more,
  merged:
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!251840](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251840),
  by @msaleiko, which adds
  `authorize_granular_token skip_reason: :parent_authorizes` to
  `WorkItemType`, `WorkItemStatus`, `WorkItemFeatures` and
  `NamespaceAvailableFeatures`, at 01:58 UTC on 2026-10-26, and
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!261599](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/261599),
  row 87's first merge request, which as merged declares
  `WorkItemSavedViewType` with a new permission, `read_work_item_saved_view`,
  at the project and group boundaries, at 04:07 UTC on 2026-10-29. Once the
  live record is taken from a release that carries them, 19.6 at the
  earliest, they retire the `WorkItemType` and `WorkItemSavedViewType` lines
  below, and the work item status this server's generated table records as
  served empty on four work item paths (create, update, a work item read and
  the listing), which a report by another user,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab#631882](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/631882)
  (opened 2026-10-02, `group::work items`), measured from the outside: a
  fine-grained token reads the status widget's `status` as `null`; @acroitor
  gave it `severity::3` and `priority::3` at 13:32 UTC on 2026-10-09, and it
  is still open and unassigned on 2026-10-31. Read from the code, not
  measured: on `master` the create, update, delete and subscribe assignables
  of the saved views do not include `read_work_item_saved_view`, and the
  create mutation declares `create_work_item_saved_view` and answers with a
  `SavedViewType`, so a saved view write by a token not granted the new
  permission still commits and answers `savedView: null`, the case the
  handlers' answer is for. Once the record is taken from such a release,
  those writes join the served writes whose object a grant can leave out,
  which `TestTable_WritesAnsweredWithoutTheirObject_AreEachAnswered` then
  holds to be declared.
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!254455](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254455),
  which declared `WorkItemType` too, was taken over by ours,
  `gitlab-org/gitlab!266046`, for the one type it had left,
  `LinkedWorkItemType`
  ([row 87](#graphql-types-and-mutations-this-server-reaches-declare-no-fine-grained-permission)).
- **Merged**: partly, unreleased: `gitlab-org/gitlab!251840` and
  `gitlab-org/gitlab!261599`, both merged by @eugielimpin in milestone 19.6,
  reached GitLab.com's production stage at 15:54 UTC on 2026-10-26 and at
  10:48 UTC on 2026-10-29. No tag carries either, so 19.6 is the first
  release that can, and the 19.5.0 table still withholds the six writes.
- **Blocking**: yes, for a fine-grained personal access token: at 19.5.0,
  19 writes cannot be served it (20 at 19.4.1; the two custom emoji writes
  left with the `CustomEmoji` declaration below, and `group.epic_create`
  joined when `WorkItem` gained the group boundary of row 89 and its answer
  stopped at `WorkItemType`).
- **Workaround**: yes. The 19 are withheld from every fine-grained session
  with the reason (register row `AUT-007`), and the reason says that GitLab
  commits such a write and answers null. Serving them would be worse than
  withholding them: a client that reads a null payload as "not done" and
  retries repeats a write GitLab already made. With the table recorded from
  19.5.0 no session that carries an authority reaches one of the 19, in any
  phase and on any release. Since issue 1103 their handlers answer the case
  all the same, for a table recorded from a later release that stops
  withholding one while a grant can still leave its object out (as the 19.5.0
  table now does for the custom emoji writes, served to a token granted
  Custom Emoji: Create alone, or such a table on an instance older than the
  declaration): an error saying
  the write was probably committed and to check before repeating it
  (`toolutil.UnconfirmedWrite`, worded by
  `finegrained.Authority.UnconfirmedWrite`). Nineteen handlers changed;
  `custom_emoji.delete`'s handler reads the errors alone and already answered a
  deletion GitLab ran as the success it is. The class is wider than the
  declarations, since a type GitLab declares and a grant does not hold answers
  the same way, and eight writes the 19.5.0 table serves reach it today: the
  four vulnerability state changes, whose Vulnerability: Update does not grant
  `read_vulnerability`, the two epic note edits, whose Work Item: Update does
  not grant `read_note`, and the two custom emoji writes, since 19.5 declares
  `CustomEmoji` and Custom Emoji: Create and Delete do not grant
  `read_custom_emoji`. Their handlers answer the same way, and
  `TestTable_WritesAnsweredWithoutTheirObject_AreEachAnswered` holds the list
  of such writes to the table. A classic token keeps the answer it had, and
  so does a fine-grained token whose kind the server could not learn, which
  carries no authority.

**Where**: `app/graphql/mutations/base_mutation.rb` and
`lib/gitlab/graphql/authz/granular_scope_authorization.rb` at `v19.4.1-ee`. A
mutation is authorized before it resolves, against its own directive, so a
grant that holds the mutation's permission passes and the write runs; the
objects of the payload are authorized after, each against its own type, and
an enforced type with no directive denies every fine-grained token, so the
payload field comes back `null` with no error.

**What**: the payload types that declare nothing at 19.5.0 and the writes
that answer with them: `Achievement` (`achievement.create`, `achievement.update`,
`achievement.delete`), `UserAchievement` (`achievement.award`,
`achievement.revoke` and the three `achievement.user_achievement_*` writes),
`WorkItemType` (`issue.work_item_create` and `group.epic_create`, through
`WorkItem.workItemType`, a non-null field whose null takes the work item with
it),
`WorkItemSavedViewType` (the four saved view writes),
`ProjectTargetBranchRule` (`project.target_branch_rule_create`),
`SecurityAttribute` (`security_attribute.create`, `security_attribute.update`)
and `SecurityCategory` (`security_category.create`,
`security_category.update`). At 19.4.1 the list held `CustomEmoji` too
(`custom_emoji.create`, `custom_emoji.delete`), which 19.5 declares. The write
is not refused, so a token that holds the mutation's permission changes GitLab
and is told nothing it can tell from a write that did not happen.

Read from the source. The same answer, a committed write and a `null`
payload with no error, was measured on a 19.4.1 instance for the group work
item of row 89, which reaches it by another path.

**How we found it**: the fine-grained derivation of issue 952, which judges a
mutation's payload as part of its answer.

**Whether GitLab means it** (issue 1103, read from GitLab's `master` at
60d9f74b2 on 2026-10-09, its specs and its tracker, and the same code at
`v19.4.1-ee`): for a read, yes. The shared example every GraphQL type is
tested with says "queries return nil values when unauthorized, mutations
raise an error"
(`spec/support/shared_examples/authz/granular_token_permissions_shared_examples.rb:41`),
[gitlab-org/gitlab!238311](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/238311),
which moved the fine-grained check onto the type, describes the `null` as the
expected answer, and
[gitlab-org/gitlab#544044](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/544044)
closed a visible error for unauthorized objects as won't do in 2025, because
an error on `project(fullPath:)` would tell a caller that a private group
exists. For a mutation's payload nothing says so, and two things point the
other way: `Mutations::BaseMutation` raises rather than answer `null` for its
own denial ("in our mutations we raise, rather than returning a null value",
`app/graphql/mutations/base_mutation.rb:29`, and "We prefer to at least say
that something went wrong", `:75-81`), and none of GitLab's fine-grained specs
of these mutations looks at the payload's object: the security attribute and
work item create specs select only `errors`, and the achievement create spec
selects the whole payload and asserts only that the payload is present, which
it is while `achievement` is `null`. So the committed write with a `null`
object is untested rather than designed.

Two things moved on `master` since 19.4.1.
[gitlab-org/gitlab!260586](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/260586)
declares `CustomEmoji` with Custom Emoji: Read at the group boundary, so
`custom_emoji.create` left the withheld set when the table was recorded from
19.5.0, and a token granted Custom Emoji: Create alone still commits the emoji
and reads `null`, which is the case the handlers' answer is for. And
`GranularScopeAuthorization#authorized?` now also judges a legacy token that
`subject_to_granular_enforcement?` (a classic token under a namespace that
enforces fine-grained tokens), so such a token reads a declared type it holds
no fine-grained permission for as `null` too, where REST answers it `403`.

**Proposal**: the declarations of row 87 for the payload types close it for
these; the class closes when a fine-grained denial is answered with an
`errors[]` entry rather than nulled. The merge request issue 1103 prepared
proposes that for every object the user's ordinary authorization admits:
`Types::BaseObject.authorized?` runs the ability check first, an object the
user cannot read stays `null` (which keeps the property the won't-do issue
above was about, and is the rule `Authz::Tokens::AuthorizeGranularScopesService#hidden_boundary`
already applies on REST), and a fine-grained denial of an object the user can
read raises a `GraphQL::ExecutionError` from `GitlabSchema.unauthorized_object`
carrying the `code` `INSUFFICIENT_GRANULAR_SCOPE` among its `extensions` and,
for a declared type, the missing permissions, behind a feature flag. A payload object denied after
the write then reads as a write that ran and returned nothing this token may
see. Lists keep their redaction in that change. Its text is kept with the
issue until it is opened.

- **Merged**: yes, in **19.5.0**, at 15:57 UTC on 2026-10-11 (merge commit

- **Blocking**: no longer. Up to the 19.4.1 table it withheld the 15 epic

  `group.epic_list`. From the 19.5.0 table `Namespace`
  ([row 87](#graphql-types-and-mutations-this-server-reaches-declare-no-fine-grained-permission))
  withholds 14 of them and that way, as it already did first, and
  `group.epic_create` stops at the `WorkItemType` its answer selects, which
  declares nothing
  ([row 88](#a-declared-mutation-whose-payload-type-declares-nothing-commits-the-write-and-answers-null)).
  Since then both are declared on `master`: `WorkItemType` by
  `gitlab-org/gitlab!251840` (merged on 2026-10-26) and `Namespace` by
  `gitlab-org/gitlab!261599` (merged on 2026-10-29), both in milestone 19.6
  and in no tag, so a record taken from a release that carries both, 19.6 at
  the earliest, should serve those actions to a grant that holds what they
  declare (inferred, not measured).
- **Workaround**: retired. Every epic position the epic actions reach was
  declared in `cmd/gen_action_grants/grant_declarations.go` (category
  `group-work-item`) as one no fine-grained token passes, and the declarations
  were removed with the re-pin; the derivation could not have reported them
  stale, since a boundary declaration is stale only when the action's
  documents stop selecting its position. Since issue 1103 the epic creation's
  handler answers a creation GitLab ran and answered without the epic as
  probably committed, which stays for the `WorkItemType` answer row 88
  describes.

**Where**: `app/graphql/types/work_item_type.rb` at `v19.4.1-ee` declares
`authorize_granular_token permissions: :read_work_item, boundary: :project,
boundary_type: :project`; re-read on `master` on 2026-10-05 (`f5d0cd38`), line
13 still declares only the project boundary. An epic is a group's work item,
whose boundary `lib/gitlab/graphql/authz/boundary_extractor.rb` cannot resolve
to a project, so the extractor returns no boundary and the service refuses
(`app/services/authz/tokens/authorize_granular_scopes_service.rb`). The
mutation `workItemUpdate` declares both the project and the group boundary
(`app/graphql/mutations/work_items/update.rb`), so the write itself passes.

**What**: measured on a 19.4.1 instance with a token granted Work Item: Read
and Work Item: Update on the epic's group: `workItem(id:)` of the epic
answers `null` with no error where a classic token reads it, and
`workItemUpdate` on it renames the epic and answers `workItem: null` with no
error. A grant on the group could therefore change an epic and never read
it. The probe in `test/e2e/gitlab/ee` holds the fixed behaviour since the
table was recorded from 19.5.0
(`TestFineGrainedProbes_GroupWorkItem_ResolvesTheGroupBoundary`): the read
answers the epic as the classic token reads it, and the write answers the
renamed epic.

**How we found it**: issue 952's derivation, read from the source, then the
probe above, which also showed the write committing where the source reading
had expected a refusal.

**Fix merged**: `WorkItem` declares `read_work_item` at the group boundary
beside the project one, as `workItemUpdate` already does, naming the
`namespace` association for the group and the `project` association for the
project rather than `resource_parent`, so that the boundary preloader keeps a
group's list of work items at the query count of `master` for either kind of
token. EE request specs pin the single work item of a group read with a token
granted on the group, the issue's query, a group's list with its projects'
work items, a token without Work Item: Read, and N+1 guards for a
fine-grained and a classic token; the fine-grained GraphQL documentation page
is regenerated with the new row. A work item in a personal namespace still
resolves no boundary, which the merge request leaves as a separate question.

### The pending-permission check exempts every type named `*Edge` or `*Payload`

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!260959](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/260959)
  ("Tell generated GraphQL types apart by class in the permission check"),
  opened from the community fork at 22:26 UTC on 2026-10-08 (one commit,
  `ed40cf7c`), the proposal below: `graphql_object_type?` leaves out a type
  that includes GraphQL Ruby's `ConnectionBehaviors` or `EdgeBehaviors`, or a
  mutation payload GraphQL Ruby generated, rather than every name ending in
  `Payload`, `Connection` or `Edge`. On the schema it was measured on, that
  leaves out the same 1587 generated types and checks four hand-written ones:
  the three below, which it adds to `authorization_todo.txt` rather than
  declare, leaving what a fine-grained token gets from them to the groups
  that own them, and `FindingDueDatesSetPayload`, which already declares a
  skip reason. It is related to
  [gitlab-org/gitlab#631631](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/631631)
  and does not close it. It was readied naming @eugielimpin, requested at
  22:34 UTC. Read at 06:42 UTC on 2026-10-09 its fork pipeline is green, and
  it has no approval and no milestone. We resolved our own threads at 19:23
  UTC that day, and at 23:25 UTC the triage bot reminded @eugielimpin that
  the review was requested more than a business day before; read on
  2026-10-10 it has no review, no approval and no milestone. The bot reminded
  @eugielimpin again at 00:28 UTC on 2026-10-12, and read that day it is
  otherwise unchanged. We asked @eugielimpin again at 00:30 UTC on
  2026-10-14; they left one non-blocking suggestion at 03:50 UTC, a comment on
  the generated type and keeping the name check, which went in as `8dfbcae3`
  at 10:23 UTC beside `b6aee867`, which passes the type's name from
  `graphql_object_type?`; they approved at 10:48 UTC.
- **Merged**: yes, unreleased: it merged at 01:43 UTC on 2026-10-15, in
  milestone 19.6, so it is not in `v19.5.0-ee` and 19.6 is the first release
  that carries it; it reached GitLab.com's production stage at 13:47 UTC that
  day.
- **Blocking**: no. No action of this server reaches any of the three types
  below.
- **Workaround**: not needed. `cmd/gen_api_live` records which types GitLab
  enforces and which declare a fine-grained permission, and the derivation
  reads that rather than GitLab's list, so these three would be judged like
  any other undeclared type.

**Where**: `graphql_object_type?` in
`lib/tasks/gitlab/permissions/graphql/schema_directives.rb` at `v19.4.1-ee`,
which the validation task (`validate_task.rb`, `current_entry_sources`) uses
to decide which types must either declare a permission or sit on
`authorization_todo.txt`, returns false for every name ending in `Payload`,
`Connection` or `Edge`.

**What**: the suffixes are meant to pass over the framing graphql-ruby
generates, but a hand-written type can carry one of those names too. Three
enforced object types that declare no permission are exempted by name and so
are on neither side of the check: `DependencyPathEdge`
(`ee/app/graphql/types/sbom/dependency_path_edge.rb`, a `BaseObject` with
the comment that authorization is on the parent),
`NamespaceWorkItemChangesPayload` and `PushEventPayload`
(`app/graphql/types/users/push_event_payload_type.rb`). A fine-grained token
reaching any of them is denied as any undeclared type is, and nothing in
GitLab's tooling lists it as pending.

**How we found it**: when the live record gained its fine-grained half,
comparing the enforced types that declare nothing with the set GitLab's own
rule computes, which the record holds beside `authorization_todo.txt`.

**Proposal**: exempt the generated connection and edge types by their class
(the types graphql-ruby builds for a connection) rather than by their name,
so a hand-written type ending in `Edge` or `Payload` is checked like any
other.

### A board name GitLab cannot save is answered as a success

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!260458](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/260458),
  "Return a 400 when a board name fails validation in the boards API", opened
  from the community fork at 18:28 UTC on 2026-10-07 and readied at 18:33 (Fix
  merged, below). No reviewer was assigned, so at 19:11 the triage bot moved
  it back to `workflow::in dev`, where it waited for a reviewer to be asked.
  One was at 22:09 UTC: a `@gitlab-bot ready @brytannia` with the `backend`,
  `type::bug` and `group::planning views` labels, since the boards moved to
  that group, set `workflow::ready for review`, and the bot requested
  @brytannia. Read on 2026-10-08 its fork pipeline is green, and it has no
  review yet, no approval and no milestone. @brytannia reviewed it that day
  with GitLab Duo (14:09 UTC, three non-blocking suggestions), approved it at
  15:51 UTC, set milestone 19.5 and passed it to @mdangelo6. Our second
  commit, `370638c4` (20:30 UTC), answers a write that fails with no
  validation errors with 400 through `bad_request!` and turns the specs into
  a table over a 256-character and an empty name, which also answers 400
  now; the push reset that approval. @mdangelo6 wrote at 00:08 UTC on
  2026-10-09 that he was "happy to accept this as a bug fix despite the
  status code rule" and approved it.
- **Merged**: yes, in **19.5.0**, tagged on 2026-10-15, and in milestone
  19.5. @mdangelo6 merged it at 01:05 UTC on 2026-10-09, on the second merge
  train run (merge commit `7038efc8`, squash commit `02e3549a`), and the
  release tooling labelled it `workflow::staging` at 06:18 UTC and
  `workflow::production` at 07:06 UTC, so GitLab.com serves it; this entry
  read it in no tag until 2026-10-16.
- **Blocking**: no, but the answer is false: a caller told the board was
  created or renamed goes on as if it were.
- **Workaround**: none taken. Neither answer says the write was dropped, and
  a length check of this server's own would copy a model validation the API
  pages do not state. The handlers report what GitLab answers: `UpdateBoard`
  in `internal/tools/boards/boards.go` and `UpdateGroupBoard` in
  `internal/tools/groupboards/group_boards.go` return the board as GitLab
  kept it, and `CreateBoard` and `CreateGroupBoard` beside them return a
  board whose ID is 0.
  `TestUpdateGroupBoard_NameGitLabCannotSave_ReturnsTheBoardGitLabKept` holds
  the update half as an instance before 19.5 answers it. From 19.5.0, the
  release the REST record is taken from, GitLab answers a name it cannot
  save on all four writes with the 400 the merge added, which the handlers
  report in GitLab's words.

**Where**: `lib/api/boards_responses.rb` at `v19.4.1-ee` (the `board`,
`create_board` and `update_board` helpers), which `lib/api/boards.rb` and
`lib/api/group_boards.rb` both include; `app/models/board.rb:14`;
`app/services/boards/create_service.rb` and
`app/services/boards/update_service.rb`.

**What**: `Board` validates a changed name at 255 characters at most
(`validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255, if:
:name_changed? }`), and nothing else checks it: the routes declare `name` a
plain `String`, the column is an unbounded `character varying`, and neither
API page states a limit. A longer name therefore fails only in the model, and
every route that sets it answers as if it had not:

- `PUT /projects/:id/boards/:board_id` and `PUT /groups/:id/boards/:board_id`
  run `update_board`, which hands `board` to `Boards::UpdateService#execute`
  (an `update` of the record, which returns false and saves nothing), then
  asks `board.valid?` and presents `board`. But `board` is a helper,
  `board_parent.boards.find(params[:board_id])`, that is not memoized, and
  `has_many :boards` (`app/models/project.rb:233`, `app/models/group.rb:111`)
  loads a new record on each `find`, so the check and the answer each read
  the stored board, which is valid because its name did not change. GitLab
  answers 200 with the board as it was, every other field of the request
  dropped with the name since the update is one save, and the
  `bad_request!("Failed to save board ...")` branch is reached by nothing the
  route accepts.
- `POST /projects/:id/boards` and `POST /groups/:id/boards` run
  `create_board`, which presents `response.payload[:board]` whatever the
  response says. `Boards::CreateService#create_board!` builds the board with
  a `create` on the parent's board collection and, when it was not persisted,
  returns `ServiceResponse.error` with the unsaved board in its payload, so
  GitLab answers 201 with a board whose `id` is `null`, and nothing is
  created.

No spec of GitLab's covers either. `spec/requests/api/boards_spec.rb` drives a
create 400 only for a missing name, which Grape answers before the helper
runs, and `spec/requests/api/group_boards_spec.rb` and the shared board
examples (`spec/support/shared_examples/requests/api/boards_shared_examples.rb`)
only a list create 400. The GraphQL board mutations report both failures in
their `errors` field (`app/graphql/mutations/boards/update.rb` and
`create.rb`), since the update reads the errors of the record it updated and
the create checks the service's response.

**How we found it**: reviewing the fix for
[issue 1213](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1213), which
had given the group board update a hint for a 400 naming the name length.
Following that 400 back through `update_board` showed GitLab never sends it,
and `create_board` beside it presents the unsaved record the same way.

**Fix merged**: all in `lib/api/boards_responses.rb`. The `board` helper is
memoized, so `update_board` presents and reports on the record the service
updated, and branches on the result of the update rather than validating the
record a second time; both helpers answer a failed write with
`render_validation_error!`, so the four routes answer
`400 {"message":{"name":["is too long (maximum is 255 characters)"]}}`, the
shape other routes use for a model that does not validate, and still save
nothing. The second commit answers a failed write that carries no
validation errors with 400 through `bad_request!` (the service's message on
create, `Failed to save board` on update), adds an empty name to the specs,
which the first commit already refuses like a long one, with `can't be
blank`, and states the 255-character limit on the `name` rows of both API
pages. The merge request treats the changed status as a bug fix, since only
a request GitLab did not save gets the new answer. 19.5.0 carries it, and
the four board handlers report GitLab's 400 as it arrives; the test and the
comments that describe the 200 as GitLab's answer are still to say it is the
answer of a release before 19.5.

**Where**: `doc/user/permissions.md`, the Project CI/CD and Project merge
requests tables, and `doc/ci/pipelines/settings.md`, the description of

**What**: the pages say what the policy does not, in four places.

- The Project CI/CD table gives the Planner role a check on seven view rows
  (the list of jobs, job logs, pipelines, viewing and downloading artifacts,
  environments, and the pipelines tab of a merge request), and no footnote
  names Planner. `config/authz/roles/planner.yml` inherits from Guest and adds
  no CI/CD read permission, so a Planner reads jobs, pipelines and artifacts
  only through `_read_public_build` and `_read_public_pipeline`, which
  `app/policies/project_policy.rb` prevents while Project-based pipeline
  visibility (`public_builds`) is off, and environments only on a public
  project.
- The View existing artifacts row gives Planner a check with no condition,
  and its footnote says a Guest sees existing artifacts only in a public
  project, while on a private one a Guest or a Planner learns of them from
  the pages the setting opens.
- The settings page said that with the setting cleared, the pipelines of an
  internal project stay visible to every authenticated user except external
  users. The pipeline list and the pipeline pages need the permission the
  setting withholds, so for those users an internal project behaves like a
  public one.
- The Project merge requests table gives Planner a check on viewing,
  searching and approving merge requests, adding internal notes and
  commenting, and nothing says a Planner loses all five when a project sets
  merge requests to Only Project Members, for which
  `ProjectFeature::PRIVATE_FEATURES_MIN_ACCESS_LEVEL` makes Reporter the
  minimum role, as the change that added the Planner role intended. The
  footnote on viewing and searching also said that an external user needs at
  least the Reporter role on an internal project, where `planner.yml` grants
  `read_merge_request` and the Planner role is enough.

The setting is on by default, so with it on a Planner does see the jobs,
pipelines and artifacts the table promises and loses only the environments of
a private project; the page was wrong for every project that turns the
setting off.

**Fix merged**: the merge request adds Planner to the footnotes of the
seven CI/CD view rows with the conditions the policy applies, gives the
environments, merge request pipelines tab and existing artifacts rows
footnotes of their own, corrects the internal-project bullet of the settings
page, adds the Only Project Members condition for Planner to five merge
request rows, and says that an external user on an internal project needs at
least the Planner role, not Reporter, to view and search merge requests. No
check mark changes.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time; a hint written from the
page would have told a Planner of a project with the setting off that it can
read the pipelines GitLab refuses it.

**How we found it**: writing the refusal hint of `pipeline.latest`'s fallback
for [issue 1234](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1234):
the CI/CD table put the lowest role that reads pipelines at Planner, and the
policy puts it at Reporter. The other statements were found reading the same
tables and the setting's page while preparing the merge request.

### The releases list caches one rendering for both values of include_html_description

- **Reported**: yes, before us, by another user:
  [gitlab-org/gitlab#588980](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/588980)
  ("REST "list releases" API doesn't split cache key on
  include_html_description"), opened on 2026-02-06, which proposes adding the
  parameter to the cache key. It was assigned to this project's maintainer
  through contributors.gitlab.com at 06:24 UTC on 2026-10-09, ten hours
  before the merge request below was opened, and was still open after the
  merge. This project's maintainer closed it at 13:51 UTC on 2026-10-17, as
  fixed by the merge request below, merged for 19.6.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!261176](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/261176)
  ("Split the releases list cache by include_html_description"), opened from
  the community fork at 16:27 UTC on 2026-10-09 (one commit, `a6333851`),
  closing that issue. The bot requested @kerrizor, who set milestone 19.5 and
  passed the review to @abignotti at 18:37 UTC as a REST API code owner, who
  passed it to @vwolanyk at 20:23 UTC while on leave. Read at 12:22 UTC on
  2026-10-10 it has a green fork pipeline, no approval, and one thread open,
  the note that passed the review on. @vwolanyk approved it at 15:06 UTC on
  2026-10-13 ("Solid change. LGTM!") and left the choice of maintainer to
  us; it was readied for @ghinfey at 16:22 UTC that day, who approved it at
  09:48 UTC on 2026-10-16.
- **Merged**: yes, unreleased: it merged at 10:46 UTC on 2026-10-16 (merge
  commit `a2ea2a19`), in milestone 19.5 but after the 19.5 cut, so it is not
  on `19-5-stable-ee` and 19.6 is the first release that carries it, unless it
  is backported; it reached GitLab.com's canary stage at 14:48 UTC that day
  and its staging stage at 15:29 UTC. Read at 15:50 UTC the issue its
  description names with `Closes` is still open, and GitLab lists no issue
  the merge request closes. It reached the production stage at 17:00 UTC
  that day, and no tag carries it yet. Read on 2026-10-31 it is in none of
  `v19.5.1-ee`, `v19.5.2-ee` and `v19.5.3-ee`, and no backport to
  `19-5-stable-ee` was opened.
- **Blocking**: no, but an answer can be wrong for five minutes:
  `release.list` with `include_html_description` set can come back without
  `description_html`, and without it set can come back with it, whenever the
  same user listed the same project's releases the other way within the
  cache's lifetime, from this server or from any other client.
- **Workaround**: none taken. The cache is GitLab's and its key cannot be
  reached from a request; the action passes the parameter through
  (`ListInput.IncludeHTMLDescription` in `internal/tools/releases/releases.go`,
  sent as `ListReleasesOptions.IncludeHTMLDescription`) and publishes
  `description_html` when the answer carries it.

**Where**: `lib/api/releases.rb`, the list route, which calls `present_cached`
with a cache context of the user alone, a lifetime of five minutes and
`include_html_description` among the presenter's options, and
`lib/gitlab/cache/helpers.rb`, which builds each cached object's key from the
presenter, the object's cache key and that context, leaving the presenter's
options out. `lib/api/entities/release.rb` exposes `description_html` only
when that option is set.

**What**: whichever request renders a release first decides what every later
request by the same user gets for five minutes. The cache came with
[gitlab-org/gitlab!60194](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/60194)
(13.12) and the parameter with
[gitlab-org/gitlab!62802](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/62802)
(14.0), which passed it to the entity without changing the key. The single
release route and the group releases list present the entity directly and
are not affected.

**Fix merged**: the merge request reads the parameter once as a boolean
and passes the same value to the cache context and to the entity, so each
variant is cached apart and an omitted parameter and `false`, which render the
same release, share an entry. Three new request specs fail on `master` and
pass on the branch.

**How we found it**: during the GitLab Hackathon of October 2026, from
GitLab's issue tracker; the issue was picked because `release.list` passes
the parameter through, which makes its answers depend on which variant the
cache holds.

### The API pages list access levels the API refuses

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below, with no issue first.
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!261285](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/261285)
  ("List only the access levels the API accepts"), opened from the community
  fork at 09:27 UTC on 2026-10-10 (one commit, `77f956a1`), documentation
  only, related to
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!248977](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/248977)
  and [gitlab-org/gitlab#301219](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/301219).
  The documentation automation requested @idurham. Read at 12:22 UTC that
  day it has a green pipeline, no approval and no milestone. @idurham
  approved it at 13:43 UTC on 2026-10-13 ("This looks good to me").
- **Merged**: yes, unreleased: @idurham merged it at 14:55 UTC on
  2026-10-13, in milestone 19.6, so it is not in `v19.5.0-ee` and 19.6 is the
  first release that carries it; it reached GitLab.com's production stage at
  03:00 UTC on 2026-10-14. It changes the pages only, so the workaround below,
  which is about this server's own schemas, is unaffected.
- **Blocking**: no, but one write is answered wrongly rather than refused.
  Most values the API refuses are answered 400 (or, adding several members
  at once, `201` with `"status":"error"` and nobody created), so nothing
  wrong is stored and the cost is a refusal a caller was told to expect to
  work. Approving an access request is the exception: the approval service
  sets the level on the request and saves it, the save fails the member's
  validation, and the route presents the unsaved record with `201`, so `0`,
  and `5` where GitLab does not accept it (on a project, or on a group that
  is not a top-level group of a licensed instance), read like an approval
  while the request stays pending. The same failed approval resolves the
  approver's to-do items and, on Enterprise Edition, records a
  `member_created` audit event. This server's two approvals used to send no
  level when given `0`, which their schemas offered as No access, so GitLab
  applied its default of `30` and the requester became a Developer, and
  reported the pending `5` as an approval.
- **Workaround**: yes, since
  [issue 1280](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1280),
  for what is ours. Every membership access level parameter is published
  from one table, `toolutil.AccessLevelSet` in
  `internal/toolutil/access_level.go`, as an integer enum and as an `N=Role`
  list in its description, held to the levels its route accepts at
  v19.5.0-ee by
  `TestBuildActionCatalog_MembershipAccessLevels_OfferOnlyWhatTheRouteAccepts`
  in `internal/tools`: the filters (`min_access_level`,
  `shared_min_access_level`, given their enum centrally) and every project
  write take Guest to Owner; the group writes (member add and update,
  invitation, both shares, SAML group link, approval) take Minimal access as
  well, described as granted only on a top-level group with a Premium or
  Ultimate license; the LDAP group link takes Minimal access on any group.
  Planner and Security Manager carry no tier any more, since Community
  Edition grants both. `access.approve_project` and `access.approve_group`
  take the level as optional, refuse before the request a level their scope
  does not grant, `0` included, and send none when it is left out; a group
  approval at `5` is refused on the Free tier without a request, reads the
  group and is refused on a subgroup before the approval, and otherwise reads
  the requester back among the group's members after it, answering a
  requester who is not found as a request still pending. The CE and EE
  end-to-end scenarios hold the three answers on a real instance.

**Where**: the `min_access_level` and `shared_min_access_level` rows of the
projects, groups, forks, starring and token association pages (14 rows), and
the `access_level` rows of the member, invitation, access request, share, LDAP
group link and SAML group link pages.

**What**: every one of those filter routes declares `values:
Gitlab::Access.all_values`, which is `10` to `50` in every edition, so `5` is
answered `min_access_level does not have a valid value`, which the merge
request measured on all 14 routes on GitLab.com while `25` answered a list;
the generated OpenAPI document already lists `10` to `50` for all 14. On the
writes, run as request specs on Community and Enterprise Edition with
`minimal_access_role` licensed and not: no route accepts `0`, the group
member update refuses `60`, `5` is accepted only on a top-level group of a
licensed Enterprise instance by the group member, invitation, access request,
group share and SAML group link routes, LDAP group links take `5` on a
top-level group and a subgroup alike, and the required `access_level` rows
document a default of `30` that does not apply.

**Fix merged**: the merge request removes `5` from the 14 filter rows and
`0` from every write row, removes `60` from the group member update row, says
where `5` is accepted, and drops the `30` defaults that do not apply. It
leaves out, to be raised on its own, that approving an access request with a
level the model refuses answers `201` with the requester while the request
stays pending.

**Beyond the merge request**: reading the routes at v19.5.0-ee for this
server's correction found two pages the merge request does not touch, the
custom role page and the broadcast message page, each listing a level the API
refuses; they are row 141,
[The custom role and broadcast message pages list a level the API refuses](#the-custom-role-and-broadcast-message-pages-list-a-level-the-api-refuses).
The same reading corrected two claims of this server's own that the pages
never made: a project access token takes Owner from a creator who holds it,
which GitLab's own service spec asserts, and a project share takes Security
Manager and Owner.

**How we found it**: checking the values this server sends against what the
API accepts, during the GitLab Hackathon of October 2026.
