### The contributed projects route writes a keyset link its finder never reads

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read in 19.4.1 and on master at `f23a2b35383` (2026-09-23),
  which carry the same lines.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `project.list_user_contributed` offers neither
  `pagination` nor `page_token`, so every surface refuses both before a request
  is sent: `ListUserContributedProjectsInput` in
  `internal/tools/projects/projects.go` carries the filters and offset
  pagination alone, and its usage line and description say the list pages by
  offset only. Until issue 1165 it published both fields, shared with the owned
  and starred lists GitLab does page by keyset, and refused them at run time.
  Beside it, `toolutil.PaginationFromResponse` withholds a next link that would
  send again the request just answered (`linkAdvances`), which stops any other
  route that behaves this way on its second reading of a page. A fix upstream
  lets the action offer keyset pagination again.

**Where**: `lib/api/projects.rb`, `GET /users/:user_id/contributed_projects`,
which builds `ContributedProjectsFinder.new(user: user, current_user:
current_user)` with no `params`, and `app/finders/contributed_projects_finder.rb`,
which reads no `id_after` or `id_before`.

**What**: the route declares `use :pagination` and presents its projects
through `present_projects`, so `pagination=keyset&order_by=id` is served by
`Gitlab::Pagination::Keyset::Pager`. That pager only limits the relation and
writes a next link naming `id_before` (or `id_after` for `sort=asc`) from the
last row; it leaves the filtering to the finder, as `ProjectsFinder` does
through `project_finder_params`. `ContributedProjectsFinder` is given no
params and filters on neither, so the request the link names answers the
first page again, under the same link. A client following GitLab's own link
reads the first page for ever; one that stops on a repeated link, as this
server does, reads it twice.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time now that the action offers
no keyset parameter; a caller pages a user's contributed projects with `page`
and `per_page`. Before the action refused keyset, a caller following
`next_page_token` read the first page twice as two pages and was then told the
listing was complete.

**How we found it**: the review of the keyset continuation of
[issue 1165](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1165), which
mocked each project list the way GitLab answers it and found that the
contributed route's link does not advance; read from the 19.4.1 source and
from master.

### The ML model package route accepts neither PRIVATE-TOKEN nor a GitLab OAuth access token

- **Reported**: no. An issue on gitlab-org/gitlab is the next step.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Measured on 19.4.2 on 2026-10-12, and read on master at
  `f23a2b35383` (2026-09-23).
- **Blocking**: yes, for an oauth HTTP mode session whose credential is a
  GitLab OAuth access token: no request this server can make downloads a model
  file with it. No for a personal access token.
- **Workaround**: yes, in part. `model_registry.download`
  (`internal/tools/modelregistry/model_registry.go`) sends the token as
  `Authorization: Bearer` on this route through
  `gitlabclient.Client.BearerToken`, beside the PRIVATE-TOKEN header the client
  sends everywhere else, so a personal access token reads the files of a
  private project. A 401 from the route in a session whose client sends Bearer
  is answered with a refusal that names this limit and the way round it, a
  personal access token (`errModelRouteRefusesOAuth`). A fix upstream retires
  both.

**Where**: `lib/api/ml_model_packages.rb`, which declares
`authenticate_with { |accept| accept.token_types(:personal_access_token,
:job_token).sent_through(:http_bearer_token) }`, and
`lib/gitlab/api_authentication/token_resolver.rb`, which resolves what that
declaration admits.

**What**: two refusals the route's own declaration produces. The first is the
header: the API guard reads only the locations a route's `authenticate_with`
names, and this one names the Bearer header alone, so a personal access token
sent as PRIVATE-TOKEN, the header GitLab documents for personal access tokens
everywhere else, leaves `current_user` nil and a private project answers 404
`Project Not Found`. On 19.4.2 the same token answers 200 as Bearer and 404 as
PRIVATE-TOKEN, for a file at the root and a nested one alike, and 200 as
PRIVATE-TOKEN on `GET /projects/:id`. The second is the token type: a Bearer
token is resolved as a personal access token and then as a job token, and a
GitLab OAuth access token is neither, so `with_job_token` raises
`UnauthorizedError` and the route answers 401 on every project, public ones
included. Nothing in the answer says why, and the route's documentation shows
Bearer without saying that it is the only header, or that an OAuth token is
not accepted.

**What it costs this server**: before the workaround, every download from a
private project read as a file that does not exist for a personal access
token, the common credential. With it, an oauth HTTP mode session holding an
OAuth access token still cannot download a model file, and is told so rather
than told its token is invalid.

**How we found it**: issue 1318, reproduced on an EE instance of the e2e
stack; the triage review read the token resolver for the OAuth half (read from
the source, not measured), and the live check of 2026-10-12 on CE 19.4.2
measured the header half for both forms of the file's path.

### SubmoduleHelper compares submodule URLs as text

- **Reported**: no. An issue on gitlab-org/gitlab is the next step.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read on master at `851b3d564ad` (2026-10-13), where the
  helper last changed on 2026-06-26.
- **Blocking**: no. GitLab's own pages leave such a submodule as plain text
  or link it to the URL as written, where a project link was due.
- **Workaround**: yes. `repository.list_submodules` and
  `repository.read_submodule_file` resolve a submodule by what its remote
  names rather than by the text GitLab compares
  (`internal/tools/repositorysubmodules/list.go`, `submoduleResolver`): a
  relative URL's containment is judged by path segment, a web clone URL is
  compared by scheme, host and port, and an SSH one by account, host and
  port. A fix upstream makes the two agree again.

**Where**: `app/helpers/submodule_helper.rb`, `relative_self_links` and
`extract_namespace_project` with `self_url?`, which decide what a submodule
links to in GitLab's pages, the repository tree among them.

**What**: two comparisons made on the URL's text where git, which fetches the
submodule, reads an address.

- `relative_self_links` refuses a relative URL whose target namespace
  `start_with?` the superproject's own path, to keep a URL inside the
  superproject from linking anywhere, since no project can live below another
  one. A string prefix also matches a sibling namespace whose name only begins
  with the superproject's: from `group/app`, `../app-tools/lib.git` lands in
  `group/app-tools`, which `"/group/app-tools".start_with?("/group/app")`
  takes for a path inside `group/app`, and the submodule is not linked. git
  fetches it from `group/app-tools/lib` on the same instance.
- `extract_namespace_project` strips `Gitlab.config.gitlab.url` or the SSH
  path prefix of the shell configuration (`ssh_path_prefix`) only when the
  URL `start_with?` it, and
  `self_url?` then compares the URL with those two strings joined to the
  project's path. A remote that names this instance in any other spelling is
  not linked: the ssh:// form of an SCP clone URL
  (`ssh://git@gitlab.example.com/group/lib.git` beside the prefix
  `git@gitlab.example.com:`), a host written in capitals, the default port
  written out (`https://gitlab.example.com:443/...`), or credentials in the
  URL. git reaches the same project through each of them.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time. This server used to follow
the helper rule for rule, which listed such a submodule as naming no project
and refused to read it, where the remote names a project on the instance that
git reads it from. It now departs from the helper on these two comparisons
only, and says so where it resolves.

**How we found it**: the review of issue 1317's resolver, which followed the
helper and found that a sibling namespace and the ssh:// spelling of the
instance's own SCP remotes, which the resolver before it read, were no longer
resolved; read from the source on master, not measured.

### The REST delete of a locked Terraform state answers 200 and deletes nothing

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read in 19.4.1.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `admin.terraform_state_delete` reads the state over
  GraphQL before it sends the delete, looking a numeric `project_id` up first
  since GitLab's GraphQL `project` field takes a path, and refuses a state
  whose `lockedAt` is set, naming `admin.terraform_state_unlock`
  (`Delete` in `internal/tools/terraformstates/terraform_states.go`). It costs
  one or two reads per delete, and a lock taken between the read and the
  delete is still answered 200; a fix upstream retires both.

**Where**: `lib/api/terraform/state.rb`, `DELETE
/projects/:id/terraform/state/:name`, which calls
`Terraform::States::TriggerDestroyService` inside
`remote_state_handler.find_with_lock` and then answers `body false` and
`status :ok` whatever the service returned.

**What**: a delete of a locked state answers 200 with an empty body (Grape's
`body false` empties the body, and `status :ok` replaces the 204 it would
set) and deletes nothing: the state is still there, and still locked, a
minute later. The route discards
the service's answer, so a caller cannot tell the refusal from the
asynchronous delete of an unlocked state, which answers the same 200 and
does complete.

**What it costs this server**: before the read-first delete, a delete of a
locked state was reported as done.

**How we found it**: issue 1327, reproduced against GitLab EE in the
`test/e2e` Docker stack: the state was still listed and locked after the 200.

### The vulnerability dismissal reason outlives the dismissal

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no. The change is one line: answer nil unless the
  vulnerability is dismissed, which is what the field's own description
  promises.
- **Merged**: no. Read in 19.4.1-ee and on master at `f23a2b35383`
  (2026-09-23), which carry the same lines.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. `vulnerabilities` publishes `dismissal_reason` only
  while the state is `DISMISSED` (`dismissalReasonWhileDismissed` in
  `internal/tools/vulnerabilities/vulnerabilities.go`), on `vulnerability.get`,
  `vulnerability.list` and the four state changes, and the card follows the
  output. A fix upstream retires it.

**Where**: `ee/app/graphql/types/vulnerability_type.rb`, whose
`dismissal_reason` returns `object.vulnerability_read&.dismissal_reason`
with no look at the state, while the field's description says "Returns null
for states other than dismissed";
`ee/app/services/vulnerabilities/base_state_transition_service.rb`, which
clears the reason only through `Vulnerabilities::Reads::UpsertService` with
`dismissal_reason: nil`; that service's `execute`, which keeps only the
projects with the `turn_off_vulnerability_read_create_db_trigger_function`
flag enabled, a GitLab.com derisk flag with `default_enabled: false`; and
the `update_vulnerability_reads_from_vulnerability` trigger in
`db/structure.sql`, which copies the severity, the state,
`resolved_on_default_branch` and `auto_resolved` to the read and never the
dismissal reason.

**What**: a vulnerability dismissed with a reason and then confirmed, resolved
or reverted to detected keeps answering that reason, with `dismissedAt`
cleared and the state the new one. On an instance where the flag is off,
which is every self-managed instance by default, nothing clears the column.

**What it costs this server**: nothing once the workaround is in. Before it,
the state changes, `vulnerability.get` and `vulnerability.list` all answered
"Dismissal Reason: FALSE_POSITIVE" beside "State: CONFIRMED", and a model read
a vulnerability it had just confirmed as a false positive.
`security_finding.list` is not affected: `PipelineSecurityReportFinding`
reads the reason from the latest state transition, which a confirm writes
without one.

**How we found it**:
[issue 1310](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1310), a
dismiss and confirm round trip on the `test/e2e` Docker stack (EE Ultimate),
then traced in the 19.4.1-ee source.

### Issue move and clone, and transfer, are authorized at the source boundary only for a fine-grained token

- **Reported**: not needed. GitLab decided this is the intended design before
  this entry was written, and documents it:
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!254840](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254840),
  merged on 2026-09-18 in milestone 19.5, added
  [the authorization principles](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/permissions/granular_access/authorization_principles/)
  for fine-grained tokens, which say the token is checked against the
  resource named in the request path and not against other resources the
  operation touches, with issue move as the example, and a section of the
  user page on
  [how fine-grained tokens authorize each request](https://docs.gitlab.com/auth/tokens/fine_grained_access_tokens/#how-fine-grained-tokens-authorize-each-request).
  The thread of that merge request records the decision as argued rather
  than unanimous: checking the target was proposed, and the cost decided it
  the other way, since a move target would have to be granted a whole
  permission group for the token's lifetime with no narrower grant
  available.
- **In review**: no, and none is coming.
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!256181](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/256181),
  merged on 2026-09-18, removed the target checks that the work item bulk
  move and the project subscription create had shipped with in 19.4, and
  [gitlab-org/gitlab!254851](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254851),
  merged on 2026-09-23, removed `additional_scopes` from the authorization of
  fine-grained tokens. Both are in milestone 19.5.
- **Merged**: no fix; the behavior is intended upstream. Read in 19.4.1 and
  in the 19.5.0-pre source, which carry the same declarations, and seen on a
  19.4.2 instance.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: none taken. Holding a move to its target would need the
  namespaces each scope of the grant names and the target's ancestry, and the
  authority this server builds from a grant deliberately keeps no namespace
  ([ADR-0024](adr/adr-0024-fine-grained-token-authority-per-action.md)), so a
  guard here needs that decision amended first. The
  [fine-grained tokens page](https://docs.jmrp.io/gitlab-mcp-server/operations/fine-grained-tokens/)
  warns that a grant does not bound where these actions write, and the
  warning stays for as long as GitLab keeps this design.

**Where**: `lib/api/issues.rb`, where the move and clone routes declare their
fine-grained permission with `boundary_type: :project` on `:id`, the project
the issue comes from; the target project reaches
`WorkItems::DataSync::MoveService` and `CloneService`, whose checks are the
user's own abilities and never the token's grant. The project and group
transfer routes (`lib/api/projects.rb`, `lib/api/groups.rb`) declare their
permission at the source in the same way.

**What**: a fine-grained token's grant scoped to selected projects decides
which projects the token may act on, and GitLab enforces it at every route by
the boundary the route declares. These routes write somewhere other than the
boundary they declare, so the place they write to is judged by the user's role
alone: a grant that names only one project does not stop an issue being moved
or cloned into another project its user can write to, although the same token
is refused on that project when it calls it directly. Transfer follows the same
pattern, and the rule GitLab documents covers it as well: the token is judged
on the resource the request path names and on nothing else the operation
reaches.

**What it costs this server**: what an operator is told a grant bounds. The
generated fine-grained table copies GitLab's declarations, so `issue.move`,
`project.transfer` and `group.transfer` are listed and called by what their
source needs, which is GitLab's rule; this server has no issue clone action.

**How we found it**: [issue 1337](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1337),
read against the 19.4.1 source and checked on a 19.4.2 instance with a token
whose grant named one project.

### The REST code search answers an exact-search name match with the path as its snippet

- **Reported**: no.
  [gitlab-org/gitlab#422752](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/422752)
  reported the same quirk in the search page, which now reads the mark, and
  was closed on 2025-05-15; the REST answer was not part of it.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read on master at `aa0991bde227` (2026-10-16).
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: yes. The code and wiki search Markdown
  (`internal/tools/search/markdown.go`, `nameMatched`) reads a result with no
  blob id whose snippet is exactly its own path as a file that matched by its
  name: its row and heading say path match, and its section says GitLab sent
  the path in place of a snippet instead of fencing the path as line 1 of the
  file. The `data` and `startline` descriptions of `search.code` say the same.
  A fix upstream that marks such a result, or answers it with the start of
  the file as basic search does, retires the reading.

**Where**: `ee/lib/search/zoekt/search_results.rb`, `build_result`, which
turns each zoekt line match into a REST result of exact code search, and
`parse_zoekt_search_result`, which makes it the `Gitlab::Search::FoundBlob`
that `API::Entities::Blob` presents.

**What**: zoekt answers a file whose name matched the query, and whose
content did not, with one line match flagged `FileName`, whose line is the
file name and which carries no line before or after it. `build_result` reads
the line and not the flag, so the result's `data` is the file's path and its
`startline` is 1 (`[LineNumber - before lines, 1].max` with a line number of
0; 19.4.1 computes `[line - 1, 0].max` and answers 0), and nothing in
`API::Entities::Blob` says the line is the file's name. The search page reads
the flag (`ee/lib/search/zoekt/multi_match.rb` skips such a match), but the
API never builds a `MultiMatch` (`search_results.rb`,
`MultiMatch.new(...) unless source == :api`), so only a REST caller is shown
the path as if it were the file's first line.

**What it costs this server**: a code search result whose snippet would read
as line 1 of the file. On gitlab.com on 2026-10-17,
`GET /projects/gitlab-org%2Fapi%2Fclient-go/search?scope=blobs&search=wikis.go`
answered `wikis.go` and `group_wikis.go` with `data` equal to the path and
`startline` 1 under `search_type=zoekt`, and with the first lines of each file
under `search_type=advanced`.

**How we found it**: the review of issue 1393's path match marker, which read
what each backend sends for a file that matched by its path.

### The custom role and broadcast message pages list a level the API refuses

- **Reported**: no. A documentation merge request on gitlab-org/gitlab, as
  for [the pages row 110 corrected](#the-api-pages-list-access-levels-the-api-refuses),
  is the next step.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read at `v19.5.0-ee` and on master at `2feb926298d5`
  (2026-10-26), where both pages still list the level.
- **Blocking**: no. GitLab answers both with `400`, so nothing wrong is
  stored, and the cost is a refusal the page told a caller to expect to work.
  Read from the code, not measured.
- **Workaround**: yes, since
  [issue 1280](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1280):
  `toolutil.CustomRoleBaseAccessLevels` and
  `toolutil.BroadcastTargetAccessLevels` in `internal/toolutil/access_level.go`
  publish what the routes accept, so `member_role.create_instance` and
  `member_role.create_group` offer Guest to Maintainer, and
  `admin.broadcast_message_create` and `admin.broadcast_message_update` every
  target but Security Manager. Nothing upstream retires it: the schemas follow
  the routes already, and a corrected page only stops disagreeing with them.

**Where**: `doc/api/member_roles.md`, the `base_access_level` row of the
custom role create, and `doc/api/broadcast_messages.md`, the list of valid
`target_access_levels`.

**What**: each page offers a level its route or its model refuses.

- `base_access_level` is listed as `10` to `50`. The create routes declare
  `values: Gitlab::Access.all_values` (`create_role_params` in
  `ee/lib/api/member_roles.rb`), which is `10` to `50`, and `MemberRole`
  validates the level against `LEVELS`, which is
  `Gitlab::Access.options_for_custom_roles`
  (`ee/app/models/members/member_role.rb`), Minimal access to Maintainer:
  Owner passes the route and fails the model, and the create answers `400`
  with the service's message. Guest to Maintainer is what both accept.
- `target_access_levels` lists Security Manager (`25`) among the valid
  levels. The create and update routes declare
  `values: System::BroadcastMessage::ALLOWED_TARGET_ACCESS_LEVELS`
  (`lib/api/admin/broadcast_messages.rb`), which is Guest, Planner, Reporter,
  Developer, Maintainer and Owner, so Grape refuses `25` with `400` before the
  model, which validates the same list, is reached.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time. Its schemas offered both
levels, because they followed the pages, and since issue 1280 they follow the
routes.

**How we found it**: reading the routes at v19.5.0-ee for issue 1280's
correction, after the merge request of
[row 110](#the-api-pages-list-access-levels-the-api-refuses) had merged.

### The API pages mark parameters for a paid tier that every tier applies, or none does

- **Reported**: no. A documentation merge request on gitlab-org/gitlab is the
  next step for the rows the source settles; it is drafted and not sent. The
  rows where the code applies a parameter its page sells as a paid feature
  are a question for GitLab before they are a merge request, since either the
  page or the missing license check can be the defect.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read at `v19.5.0-ee` and on master on 2026-10-27, where
  every row below still carries its tier.
- **Blocking**: no. A tier marker on a parameter every tier applies hides it
  from nobody who reads the code, and the two filters no tier reads were
  answered with every project rather than refused. The cost is a schema that
  followed the page.
- **Workaround**: yes, since
  [issue 1240](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1240):
  each row is answered in `cmd/audit_edition_tier/param_declarations.go`
  with the source line that settles it, or, for a parameter no tier honors,
  removed from the input. Nothing upstream retires it: a corrected page only
  stops disagreeing with the schemas.

**Where and what**, read against GitLab's Grape params and services:

- The source settles the row, and the page is what is wrong:
  - `doc/api/groups.md`, `marked_for_deletion_on` on the group list: Community
    Edition declares and applies it (`lib/api/groups.rb:37`, whose own
    description repeats the tier, and `app/finders/groups_finder.rb:158-162`).
  - `doc/api/group_level_variables.md`, `filter` on the get, update and
    delete: read from the raw params on every tier and edition
    (`lib/api/helpers/variables_helpers.rb:16-22` and
    `app/finders/ci/variables_finder.rb:26-29`).
  - `doc/api/notification_settings.md`, `new_epic` in the table the page
    shares between the group and the project update: a project's update does
    not declare it (`EE::NotificationSetting::EMAIL_EVENTS_MAPPING`,
    `ee/app/models/ee/notification_setting.rb:7-17`), so the row is the
    group's alone.
  - `doc/api/projects.md`, `repository_checksum_failed` and
    `wiki_checksum_failed` on the project lists: declared
    (`ee/lib/ee/api/helpers/projects_helpers.rb:38-42`) and read by nothing,
    so the filter returns every project on every tier.
  - `doc/api/projects.md`, `auto_duo_code_review_enabled` on the update,
    "Ultimate only": the update keeps it where the instance's license carries
    `review_merge_request`, a Premium feature, and the project has Duo code
    review (`ee/lib/ee/api/helpers/projects_helpers.rb:144-149`).
- Enterprise Edition applies the parameter on every tier with no license
  check, while the feature page sells it as Premium:
  - `doc/api/groups.md`, `membership_lock` on the create and update (only the
    settings page checks `member_lock`), and both compute minute limits,
    which an administrator sets on every tier
    (`ee/app/services/ee/groups/update_service.rb:80-86`).
  - `doc/api/remote_mirrors.md`, `mirror_branch_regex` on the push mirror
    create and update (`ee/lib/ee/api/helpers/remote_mirrors_helpers.rb:11-14`
    and `ee/app/models/ee/remote_mirror.rb:22-35`).
  - `doc/api/projects.md`, `include_hidden` on the project list, kept for an
    administrator (`ee/lib/ee/api/projects.rb:116-121`).

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time now. Its schemas followed
the pages, and since issue 1240 they follow the routes: the rows above are
declared, `new_epic` is offered only where it is declared, and the two
checksum filters are offered by no list.

**How we found it**: answering the 65 parameter findings of
`make audit-edition-tier` for issue 1240, each read against the source at
v19.5.0-ee.

### The service account token list examples sort by a value their pages do not list

- **Reported**: no.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read at `v19.5.0-ee` and on master at `a728284cfb1d`
  (2026-10-27), which carry the same lines.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: none. `group.service_account_pat_list` and
  `project.service_account_pat_list` publish `sort` as the eight orders the
  pages list (the `SchemaEnumOverride` in `action_specs.go` of
  `internal/tools/groupserviceaccounts` and
  `internal/tools/projectserviceaccounts`), as the three access token lists
  do, so the example's `id_desc` is not among the values they offer. A fix
  upstream that says which orders the routes take decides whether that enum
  grows.

**Where**: `doc/api/service_accounts.md`, the sections that list the personal
access tokens of a group service account and of a project service account.
Each attribute table gives `sort` eight possible values, and the example
request under it sends `?sort=id_desc`. The code behind both routes is
`access_token_params` in `lib/api/helpers/personal_access_tokens_helpers.rb`,
which declares `sort` as a `String` with no `values`,
`PersonalAccessTokensFinder#sort` in `app/finders/personal_access_tokens_finder.rb`
and `PersonalAccessToken.simple_sorts` in `app/models/personal_access_token.rb`.

**What**: the finder sorts by any key of `PersonalAccessToken.simple_sorts`
and leaves the tokens unsorted for any other value. That hash merges the eight
documented orders over `Sortable.simple_sorts`
(`app/models/concerns/sortable.rb`), so it holds seventeen keys: the eight,
and `id_asc`, `id_desc`, `created_at_asc`, `created_at_desc`, `created_date`,
`updated_asc`, `updated_desc`, `updated_at_asc` and `updated_at_desc`. The
example's `id_desc` is one of the nine the pages do not list: it sorts, but a
reader cannot tell from the page whether it is supported. Since the route declares no `values`, a value outside all
seventeen, such as `asc`, is accepted and ignored. The personal, project and
group access token pages list the same eight values, and their examples send
no `sort`.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time. The enum follows the
documented list and leaves out the nine undocumented orders, the example's
`id_desc` among them, so a caller cannot ask these two lists for the tokens by
id until GitLab says that order is supported.

**Proposal**: a documentation merge request changing both examples to a
listed order, such as `created_desc`, the example `access_token_params` itself
documents. Listing the nine as well, or declaring `values` on `sort` so that
an order the finder does not apply is refused with 400, is GitLab's choice;
the first would let the enum here grow, and the second would make GitLab
refuse `asc` and `desc` as the schema here does.

**How we found it**: the review of
[issue 1165](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1165)'s
first layer, which replaced the two lists' `asc` and `desc` enum with the
documented orders and read the finder to see which values GitLab applies.

### A merge request creation can be refused for a branch that exists, from a stale branch name cache

- **Reported**: yes, by GitLab,
  [gitlab-org/gitlab#506430](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/506430)
  ("`Gitlab::RepositorySetCache#fetch` is not atomic"), opened on 2024-11-26
  with a spec that reproduces the race and names `branch_names_include?` as a
  check it makes answer wrongly. Read at 21:55 UTC on 2026-10-31: open,
  `type::bug` and `severity::4`, no assignee, milestone 19.6 after
  `missed:19.2` to `missed:19.5`. We have written nothing on it.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. Read at `v19.5.3-ee`, the release the run below tested.
  Two flags would each take the merge request validation off the racing
  cache, and both are off by default there: `ref_existence_check_gitaly`
  (beta, since 18.4), which answers `Repository#branch_exists?` from Gitaly,
  and `ref_cache_with_rebuild_queue` (work in progress, since 18.9).
- **Blocking**: no. The tools send the creation and report GitLab's refusal;
  what it failed was the e2e suite, twice.
- **Workaround**: yes, in the e2e fixture only. `fixture.NewMergeRequest`
  (`test/e2e/internal/fixture/merge_request.go`) reads a `400` whose
  validation errors say a branch "does not exist", drains Sidekiq, asks
  `HEAD /projects/:id/repository/branches/:branch` until it answers a success,
  and tries the creation again; a branch the cache does not list within 30
  seconds (60 on a licensed instance) fails the test with GitLab's refusal
  after one wait. The two scenarios that create a merge request through the
  server right after a branch and a commit of their own
  (`TestMergeRequest_Create_FromABranchWithACommit` and the merge request of
  `b7_issue_relations_test.go`) do not retry it. What retires the workaround
  is a release the suite runs against that carries a fix, or either flag on
  by default.

**Where**: `MergeRequest#validate_branch_existence`
(`app/models/merge_request.rb`, `validate ... on: :create`) adds
`does not exist` for each branch `nonexistent_branches` names, which asks
`Repository#branch_exists?` (`app/models/repository.rb`). With
`ref_existence_check_gitaly` off that is `branch_names_include?`
(`lib/gitlab/repository_cache_adapter.rb`), a membership test of the Redis set
`Gitlab::RepositorySetCache#fetch` (`lib/gitlab/repository_set_cache.rb`)
fills, reading Gitaly only when the set does not exist. `lib/api/helpers/merge_requests_helpers.rb`
answers the error as `400 {"message":{"source_branch":["does not exist"]}}`.
The commits API checks the same cache before a write
(`Commits::CreateService`, "You can only create or edit files when you are
on a branch"), and so does `HEAD /projects/:id/repository/branches/:branch`
(`lib/api/branches.rb`), while the `GET` of the same path reads the branch
from Gitaly.

**What**: `fetch` reads the set, and when it is missing lists the branches
from Gitaly and writes the list back, with no check that the set was not
emptied in between. Creating a branch empties the set synchronously
(`Repository#after_create_branch`), and every push's PostReceive job empties
and refills it under a lease (`Repositories::PostReceiveWorker#expire_branch_cache`,
whose comment describes the race between two such jobs). A request or a job
that started listing before the branch was created and writes after the set
was emptied leaves a list without the branch, and every check that reads the
cache says the branch does not exist until the next PostReceive refills it.
`MergeRequests::BuildService#ref_exists_in_gitaly?` covers that mismatch for
the web form ("fallback if there is a mismatch between the cache and
repository state"), and the API creation does not go through it. On the
release rehearsal of 2026-10-31, against GitLab 19.5.3,
`TestCommit_Rewrite_CherryPicksRevertsAndFindsMergeRequests/individual`
created a branch, committed to it on the first attempt and was refused the
merge request from it 1.8 seconds after the subtest began, project 58
answering `400 {message: {source_branch: [does not exist]}}`; the commit had
passed the same cache check moments before, so the stale list landed between
the two. The weekly e2e run of 2026-10-26 failed the same test the same way
on its meta subtest. Both failures came on the second or third surface of a
project the scenario shares across surfaces, where the previous surface's
pushes, pipelines and merge request are still being processed. In the same
rehearsal `TestMergeRequest_Create_FromABranchWithACommit/individual` met the
commits API's form of the refusal, which its retry waited out in under two
seconds.

**What it costs this server**: nothing at run time it can avoid. A client that
creates a merge request right after creating its branch can be refused for a
branch that exists, and is told GitLab's refusal as it came; asking again a
few seconds later works.

**Proposal**: none of ours. The issue carries the reproduction, and the fix
is GitLab's choice among a write that cannot overwrite a newer emptying, the
rebuild queue behind `ref_cache_with_rebuild_queue`, or
`ref_existence_check_gitaly` on by default.

**How we found it**: the e2e gate of the release rehearsal of 2026-10-31,
whose failure was read against GitLab's source at `v19.5.3-ee`.

## GitLab Orbit (`gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph`)

The first two entries here were filed as an issue first and then a merge
request that closes it, because the project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for an
issue before any non-trivial merge request; the third, a CI job's defect, went
out as a merge request alone and touches only `.gitlab-ci.yml`. Each of the
first two merge requests bumps the Orbit skill to `0.32.3`, as every change
under `skills/orbit/` must, so whichever lands second needs `0.32.4`.
Nothing in the project's pipeline will flag it: the two branches merge
cleanly, since both make the same change to the version, and
`skill-version-bump-check` compares a branch with its merge request's diff
base, where the skill stays at `0.32.2` until the branch is rebased. The
commit that updated each branch's tests (below) says so in its message. The
numbers have moved since: on 2026-10-01 both branches were rebased onto a
`main` where
[gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph!2672](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/merge_requests/2672),
merged that day, had taken the skill to `0.33.0` and added a GQL copy,
`SKILL.gql.md`, versioned as the JSON skill's version plus
`+gql`, and they took `0.33.1` and `0.33.2`, each with the four tests that pin
the two versions. Row 75's merged at `0.33.1`, and row 76's was rebased onto
that on 2026-10-02 and keeps `0.33.2`, one above `main`. On 2026-10-02
[gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph!2692](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/merge_requests/2692)
stopped those tests hardcoding the version, so a bump no longer edits them.

- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: not needed. `orbit.dsl` handed the model GitLab's schema text
  verbatim, which states the rule, and `orbit.query`'s own guidance stated
  it too since
  [issue 1031](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1031): its
  parameter guidance named `rel_types` as required, `["*"]` for any type, and
  the Orbit live suite held a path query naming them to a 200. Since
  2026-10-15 GitLab.com reads every query as GQL, and read on 2026-10-17
  `GET /orbit/schema/dsl` answers 404, so the JSON schema this row is about
  is no longer what a GitLab.com caller writes against. In GQL a shortest
  path names its relationship type in the pattern,
  `-[:IN_PROJECT*1..2]->`, which is what `orbit.query` teaches and the live
  suite asks since
  [issue 1414](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1414).
  That issue also taught any type, `-[*1..3]->`, for a shortest path, which
  lowers to `rel_types` `["*"]` and so met this row's rule. Since
  [gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph!3075](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/merge_requests/3075)
  ("fix(compiler): tighten query validation", merged on 2026-10-26, first in
  Orbit v0.159.0) the rule is stricter: the compiler refuses a wildcard,
  `["*"]` or no type at all, where it refused only a missing `rel_types`
  before, and GitLab.com answered such a shortest path with "shortest paths
  require named relationship types" on 2026-10-26 and again on 2026-10-29.
  `orbit.query` says a shortest path names its types, and the live suite asks
  one that does, since
  [issue 1528](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1528),
  closed by pull request 1585 on 2026-10-29.

**Where**: `PathConfig.rel_types.description` in
`config/schemas/graph_query.schema.json` (main `1c43d9f0`, line 636), served
verbatim by `GET /orbit/schema/dsl`; the same statement in the query language
guide (`docs/source/remote/queries/query-language.md:566,568-570`), its copy in
the Orbit skill and the skill's path recipe (`recipes.md:419-420`).

**What**: they say `rel_types` is optional when both endpoints use `node_ids`.
The validator (`check_path` in
`crates/query-engine/compiler/src/passes/validate.rs:1221-1231`) has rejected
every path query without it since
[gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph!1621](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/merge_requests/1621)
(2026-06-09), and its own test pins the `node_ids` case. On GitLab.com the
query the schema allows answers `400` with "path_finding requires rel_types to
bound fan-out". The guide's path example also runs from a project to a user
through relationship types that point the other way, so it returns no rows;
reversed, the same query returns two paths.

**Fix merged**: the merge request states the rule in the schema, the guide,
the skill copy and the recipe, turns the guide's example round, and bumps the
skill. It changes no accepted query, so it left the `query_dsl` version
alone and put that choice, and making `rel_types` required in the schema
itself, to the maintainers in the issue. Its review suggested the second,
which the follow-up above did; it merged on 2026-10-05.

**How we found it**: sending the query the description allows to GitLab.com
while rewriting `orbit.query` for issue 1031.

  change stayed the same. The note posted with the second rebase (17:43 UTC)

  head `f1db93a2`. Its fork pipeline, 2913907361, passed, `lint:prose`
  included, the first fork pipeline of this merge request in which that job
  ran to the end. A note at 14:42 UTC in the thread our rebase note of
  2026-10-02 opened, where @aalgutifan had asked for the last rebase

- **Merged**: yes, at 16:21 UTC on 2026-10-05, by @aalgutifan, as squash
  commit `20080819` (merge commit `fc57ab46`). It is in **v0.137.0**, cut the
  same day (release commit `1872b6f9`, 17:08 UTC), and GitLab.com serves it:
  read at 21:06 UTC on 2026-10-05, `/orbit/status` reports Orbit 0.137.0 and
  `NeighborsConfig.direction` in `/orbit/schema/dsl` declares
  `"default": "outgoing"` and describes the default as `outgoing`. Read on
  2026-10-16, GitLab.com serves Orbit 0.145.0, its newest tag.
- **Blocking**: no. Until the release a result could be silently incomplete,
  to a client that read the schema's default.
- **Workaround**: not needed. GitLab.com's schema stated the default, and
  `orbit.query`'s own guidance said it too since
  [issue 1031](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1031):
  the schema description of `query`, its parameter guidance and the site's
  Orbit page each said that `direction` defaults to `outgoing` and to pass
  `both` for every relationship of the center, and the Orbit live suite asked
  its neighbors queries that way. Since 2026-10-15 GitLab.com reads every
  query as GQL, and read on 2026-10-17 `GET /orbit/schema/dsl` answers 404.
  In GQL the direction is written in the pattern, the undirected `--` for
  every relationship of a node and `->` or `<-` for one direction, which is
  what `orbit.query` teaches and the live suite asks since
  [issue 1414](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1414).

**Where**: `NeighborsConfig.direction` in
`config/schemas/graph_query.schema.json` (main `1c43d9f0`, lines 654 to 658)
declares `"default": "both"` and describes the default as `both`, while the
shared `Direction` definition in the same file and the compiler
(`crates/query-engine/compiler/src/input.rs:446-452` and `882-888`) default to
`outgoing`.

**What**: on GitLab.com a neighbors query without `direction` returns only the
relationships that start at the center node, exactly as `outgoing` does, and
nothing in the answer says the incoming ones were left out: a project's
neighbors are its branches, and its group, creator and labels appear only with
`"direction": "both"`.

**Fix merged**: the merge request documents `outgoing` in the schema and
adds `direction` and `rel_types` to the guide's neighbors section and its
skill copy. Making `both` the compiler's default instead would change what
existing queries return, so it was left in the issue as the maintainers'
choice, and the merge closed the issue without taking it.

**How we found it**: comparing a neighbors query with and without
`direction` against GitLab.com while checking the schema for issue 1031.

### The pinned version check stops with "no merge base" on forks and long branches

- **Reported**: yes, by the merge request below, with no issue first,
  although the project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for one before any
  non-trivial merge request (the section's introduction); its description
  says "Related Issues: None".
- **In review**: yes,
  [gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph!2746](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/merge_requests/2746)
  ("fix(ci): stop pinned-version-check failing with no merge base"), opened
  from the community fork at 22:24 UTC on 2026-10-08 (one commit,
  `90941495`) and readied at 22:27 naming @dgruzd, who is its reviewer. Read
  at 06:42 UTC on 2026-10-09 its fork pipeline was green, and it had no
  approval and no milestone. At 12:26 UTC @dgruzd set milestone 19.6 and
  approved it with one non-blocking suggestion, a shorter comment, which went
  in as `0137e69d` at 16:54 UTC; he set it to merge at 16:59 UTC.
- **Merged**: yes, at 17:23 UTC on 2026-10-09, by @dgruzd (merge commit
  `b7966dcf`), on `main` and in milestone 19.6. It changes the CI only, so no
  release has to carry it; it came after v0.139.0, and read on 2026-10-16 it
  is in every tag from v0.140.0 to v0.145.0, the newest. Read on 2026-10-31
  it is in every tag through v1.0.0 (2026-10-29), the newest, and the job on
  `main` still compares against the two SHAs it introduced.
- **Blocking**: no. It costs this server nothing; it fails the fork pipelines
  of a contribution such as rows 75 and 76 before the check has looked at
  anything.
- **Workaround**: none needed. A failed run of the job on a fork says nothing
  about the change, and a pipeline in the canonical project, or a rebase,
  gives the real answer.

**Where**: the `pinned-version-check` lint job of the project's CI and
`scripts/checks/check-pinned-version.sh` on `main`, where `5aeca777`
("refactor(ci): group scripts by role and remove dead files", 2026-10-10)
moved it from `scripts/`, the sibling of the
`skill-version-bump-check` job the section's introduction describes.

**What**: the runner clones a merge request pipeline at depth 20; the job
fetched the target branch at depth 1 and ran
`git diff --name-only origin/<target>...HEAD`, which needs a merge base. It
stops with "no merge base" in a detached pipeline, every fork pipeline among
them, once the target has moved past the branch's base or when the branch is
longer than the clone depth, and in a merged results pipeline whose target
moved after GitLab made the merge commit. The merge request counts 13
failures of this job in the community fork since 2026-09-20, 9 of them on
"no merge base", and 120 in the project's 1,500 most recent failed jobs, 49
of them on "no merge base" across 18 merge requests.

**How we found it**: the fork pipelines of the merge requests of rows 75 and
76, which failed this job that way.

**Fix merged**: the job compares against `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_SHA`
in a merged results pipeline and `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA` otherwise,
commits the pipeline's commit descends from, and fetches the rest of the
branch's history by its SHA only when the base is outside the clone; the
script itself is unchanged. The description sets out why the diff base alone,
the way `skill-version-bump-check` fetches it, fixes neither a long detached
branch nor a merged results pipeline.

  merged at 20:18 UTC on 2026-10-19 as `b732e703`, which replaces
  `golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp` with `github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto`. The
  maintainer had answered on 2026-08-05 that the change is breaking by Go's
  convention and would need a v2 of the module; it went into the v1 module
  instead.
- **Merged**: **yes, v1.7.0**, tagged at 21:26 UTC on 2026-10-19, with no
  GitHub release page for it.
- **Blocking**: no.
- **Workaround**: retired. It was the `GO-2026-5932` entry in the govulncheck
  allowlist. Removing the self-update subsystem in 3.0.0 took the openpgp
  import out of every binary, so the source scan has reported nothing since
  and the allowlist is empty again. The module itself stayed in the binaries
  of 3.0.0 and 3.1.0, through the HKDF import in `internal/telemetry`, and a

  `make check-binary-vulns` holds every release binary to the database at

### gobco type-checks every file of a package directory, whatever its build constraints say

- **Reported**: yes,
  [rillig/gobco#40](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/40), opened
  2026-09-28 with a minimal reproduction of the panic and of four related cases.
- **In review**: yes,
  [rillig/gobco#41](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/41), opened the same
  day from a fork: two commits, one per half of the fix, each with its tests.
  The project's CI never ran on it: its Go workflow run (36452317634,
  2026-09-28) waited on the maintainer's approval, as a first contribution's
  does, still read `action_required` on 2026-10-13, and ended without it at
  16:43 UTC on 2026-10-28, thirty days after it was created, with conclusion
  `failure` and no job. A reminder at 18:08 UTC on 2026-10-19
  ([comment 6273951341](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/41#issuecomment-6273951341)),
  which also names [rillig/gobco#43](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/43),
  said both still merge cleanly and offered the maintainer's own commits
  instead; read on 2026-10-31 it has no answer.
- **Merged**: no. Up to 2024 the maintainer fixed an issue that carried a
  reproduction directly, within days, with a commit of his own, and one pull
  request has ever been merged as sent, in 2019, so the fix may well arrive
  as the maintainer's own commit. The 2026 record is slower: the fix for
  [rillig/gobco#38](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/38) landed on
  `master` three days after the report, on 2026-05-03, with the maintainer
  offering a release once the snapshot worked for its reporter. It did not:
  on 2026-05-04 the reporter showed the snapshot (`7a099954`, the commit read
  under Where below) still panicking in `resolveTypes`, with "could not
  import" errors from the source importer, the type-checking step v1.3.4
  introduced and this entry's issue is about, and the maintainer reopened the
  issue on 2026-05-06, so the release offered there waits on the same path
  as this entry. No release has been tagged since v1.3.4 (2024-03-08),
  `master` being 9 commits ahead of it when read on 2026-10-05, when this
  entry's issue and pull request still had no response. Read again on
  2026-10-07 and on 2026-10-13, nothing has moved: v1.3.4 is still the newest
  tag, `master` is still 9 commits ahead at `7a099954`, and the issue and the
  pull request are open with no comment, review, label or assignee. Read on
  2026-10-31, v1.3.4 is still the newest tag and `master` is still 9 commits
  ahead at `7a099954`; the issue has no comment, and the pull request none
  but the reminder above. Either way the entry retires on the release that
  carries the fix, and it is re-read at each gobco tag.
- **Blocking**: no for the server. It blocked the condition gate on three
  packages: `cmd/server` and `internal/toolutil` panicked before anything was
  instrumented, and `test/e2e/internal/harness` with `-tags=e2e` was never
  instrumented at all. With the workaround below only the harness is left
  unmeasured.
- **Workaround**: partial.
  [Issue 1017](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1017)
  measures such a package from a copy of the module that leaves out the files
  the go command does not build here and blanks the constraint lines gobco's
  narrow build context would misread, which is what the fix does inside gobco:
  `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh`, run by `make coverage-conditions` and by
  `scripts/check-spec-conditions.sh`, measures `cmd/server` at 2236 of 2236
  conditions and `internal/toolutil` at 3870 of 3870 on linux/amd64. The
  harness is not measured: every file of it sits behind `e2e`, so blanking
  its constraints fails its own test that each file carries exactly that
  line, and the script says the figure it printed is not a measurement. The
  platform halves the copy leaves out (four source files of `cmd/server`, two
  of `internal/toolutil`) are measured on the platforms that build them: the
  Windows and macOS legs of CI's cross-platform job run the same script on
  both packages and fail on a condition left one-way in a file Linux does not
  build. It retires when a gobco release carries the fix and the pin,
  `github.com/rillig/gobco@v1.3.4` in `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh`
  (its `GOBCO` constant), moves to it. That change, once the release exists,
  does four things. It moves the pin and measures
  `test/e2e/internal/harness` directly with `TAGS=e2e`, which under the pull
  request's build gave 863 of 1162 conditions; once measurable, the harness is held to the gate like any
  package a change touches, which means closing its one-way conditions. It
  retires the staged module copy and its constraint blanking from
  `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh`, with the text that describes them: the
  script's header (which says the harness waits for gobco to honour build
  tags), the staging note of `scripts/check-spec-conditions.sh`, and the two
  paragraphs of `docs/development/testing/README.md` that begin "gobco reads
  a package as every `.go` file" and "The e2e harness stays unmeasured until
  gobco honours build tags". It exempts the `gobco_*.go` files gobco generates
  from `TestSources_EveryFile_CarriesExactlyTheE2EConstraint`
  (`test/e2e/internal/harness/sources_test.go`), which is ours to do and would
  be dead code before the release, since the staged copy blanks the
  constraint lines that test reads. And it marks this entry merged with the
  gobco version, keeping it. Moving the coverage recipes into a Go command
  ([issue 1114](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1114),
  open) carries the pin with them; if gobco releases first, that command need
  not stage at all.

**Where**: `rillig/gobco` at `7a09995` (v1.3.4 behaves the same).
`instrumenter.instrument` hands every `.go` file of the directory to
`parser.ParseDir` (`instrumenter.go:87-94`), whose filter only narrows the set
to one file named on the command line, and `resolveTypes` type-checks all of
them as one package (`instrumenter.go:142`), which v1.3.4 introduced
(`09623a7`); v1.3.3 resolved no types. `shouldBuild` matches files against a
build context holding only `GOOS` and `GOARCH` (`instrumenter.go:1001`), so
no build tag and no release tag counts, and the source importer resolves
imports in `build.Default` (`instrumenter.go:114`), which knows nothing of
the tags gobco passes on to `go test`.

**What**: a package that implements a function once per platform, the usual
Go idiom, makes gobco panic with "redeclared in this block" while `go test`
passes on the same package. The same cause shows four more ways: a
`//go:build ignore` generator with `package main` beside the package makes
gobco write a bridge test with `import  ""`; a `TestMain` in another platform's
test file keeps gobco from adding its own, and the report is
`Condition coverage: 0/0` with exit status 0; files built only with `-tags` are
never instrumented, not even with `-test -tags=...`; and a black box test of
such a package panics with "could not import".

**Fix in review**: the pull request selects files with `build.Default.MatchFile`
before parsing, which also skips names starting with `_` or `.` and honours
release tags, and takes the build tags from `GOFLAGS` and the `-test` options
the way the go command does, setting them in `build.Default.BuildTags` while
the package is instrumented, since `importer.ForCompiler` takes no other
build context. No dependency is added, and `sh ./test.sh` passes with Go
1.16.15, 1.20.14 and 1.27.1. With it, gobco measures this repository's three
packages: `cmd/server` 1990 of 2032 conditions and `internal/toolutil` 3604 of
3782, the same figures the copy of issue 1017 gives, and
`test/e2e/internal/harness` with `-tags=e2e` 863 of 1162. That last run fails
one test of ours,
`TestSources_EveryFile_CarriesExactlyTheE2EConstraint`, because the files gobco
generates carry no `//go:build e2e`; exempting gobco's files there is ours to
do.

**How we found it**: the condition gate reported `cmd/server` as not measured
([issue 1017](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1017)), and
reproducing the panic outside this repository showed where it comes from.

**Where it was tracked**: issue 1017's Linux half was done by pull request
1064 and its Windows and macOS legs by pull request 1206; what waited on gobco
was split into
[issue 1099](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1099), a
watch re-read at each gobco tag, which this entry replaced when it closed on
2026-10-07. That issue also carried a second gobco limit with the same owner,
which had no entry until then and is
[entry 97](#gobco-cannot-instrument-a-package-whose-export_testgo-feeds-its-external-test-package).

### gobco cannot instrument a package whose export_test.go feeds its external test package

- **Reported**: yes,
  [rillig/gobco#42](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/42),
  opened on 2026-10-08 with a minimal reproduction. It is neither the fourth case of
  [rillig/gobco#40](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/40), which is the
  build-tag one
  ([entry 73](#gobco-type-checks-every-file-of-a-package-directory-whatever-its-build-constraints-say)),
  nor [rillig/gobco#33](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/33) with its
  open fix [rillig/gobco#39](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/39), which
  are about finding the import path of a black box test's package. Searched
  on 2026-10-07 and again on 2026-10-08 before it was opened, gobco's tracker
  had no issue or pull request about
  `export_test.go` or an external test package's symbols.
- **In review**: yes,
  [rillig/gobco#43](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/43),
  opened on 2026-10-08 from the branch `export-test-package` of
  `jmrplens/gobco` (`1b7a942`, one commit on `master` at `7a09995`).
  Decided on 2026-10-06, in the maintainer's comment on
  [issue 1099](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1099):
  this gets a fix and a pull request to gobco, not a workaround in this
  repository's staging script. That comment scheduled both for after the
  gobco release carrying entry 73's fix; on 2026-10-08 the maintainer
  decided to open them before any release, with entry 73's pull request
  still unreviewed. The fix is independent of that pull request: both touch
  `instrumenter.go`, `instrumenter_test.go` and `main_test.go`, and git
  merges the two branches without a conflict. Read on 2026-10-09 and again on
  2026-10-13, its Go workflow run (37855282392) waits on a maintainer's
  approval to run, as entry 73's (36452317634) has since 2026-09-28, it has
  no review, and both pull requests still merge onto `master` without a
  conflict. Read on 2026-10-31, its run still reads `action_required`, while
  entry 73's ended unapproved on 2026-10-28, thirty days after it was created
  (entry 73, In review); the reminder of 2026-10-19 on
  [rillig/gobco#41](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/41#issuecomment-6273951341)
  names this pull request too, and has no answer, and GitHub still reports
  both pull requests mergeable. The decision of 2026-10-06 against a workaround in the staging
  script is superseded by the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-27 to carry
  one until gobco releases the fix (Workaround, below); the fix and its pull
  request stand.
- **Merged**: no.
- **Blocking**: no for the server. It kept the condition gate from measuring
  a package it reaches until the workaround below. `scripts/check-spec-conditions.sh` reported such a
  package as not measured and did not fail on it, and
  `docs/development/testing/README.md` said the same; both counted 25 of the
  169 packages carrying an `action_specs.go` as in that state, a figure from
  when they were written and not measured again then (read from the tree on
  2026-10-07 and again on 2026-10-13, 22 of the 150 `action_specs.go` files sit beside an
  `export_test.go` whose package also has an external test package).
  `internal/clientcompat` is held by mutation testing instead (pull request
  1047), and `internal/tools/issues` was measured once, 368 of 368
  conditions, only through a workaround applied by hand to a copy of the
  module outside this repository (pull request 1067), which the
  repository's tooling did not carry until the workaround below.
- **Workaround**: yes, since 2026-10-27, and temporary. On 2026-10-27 the
  maintainer decided to keep it until gobco publishes a release with the fix,
  which supersedes the decision of 2026-10-06 (In review, above) that left
  this to gobco. The whole-tree measurement of 26 October 2026 found 27 packages in
  this state (`docs/development/testing/README.md`, The whole tree), and the
  OpenSSF Best Practices gold criterion `test_branch_coverage80` asks for a
  figure over the whole tree, which waited on a release that has not come.
  `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh` stages such a package: in its copy of the
  module, each test file of the package that declares no test, benchmark,
  fuzz test or example becomes a file of the package, renamed without its
  `_test` suffix and opened with `//go:build gc`, which the go command
  satisfies and gobco's own narrower build context does not, so it is
  compiled into the test binary as before, its names reach the black box
  test, and gobco leaves it uninstrumented, as it leaves a test file. It
  moves no position gobco reports. The 27 are measured that way, the 22
  `action_specs.go` packages among them. The staging goes when gobco
  publishes a release carrying the fixes,
  [rillig/gobco#43](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/43) for
  [rillig/gobco#42](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/42) and
  [rillig/gobco#39](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/39) for entry 140's
  [rillig/gobco#33](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/33), and the pin of
  entry 73 moves to it, with the paragraph of
  `docs/development/testing/README.md` that describes it.

**Where**: `rillig/gobco` at `7a09995` (`master`, read on 2026-10-07),
`resolveTypes` (`instrumenter.go:113-150`). It type-checks each package of the
directory with `importer.ForCompiler(fset, "source", nil)`. When it checks the
external `x_test` package, that importer loads `x` from `build.Default`,
which reads the non-test files of a directory only, so a symbol `x`'s
`export_test.go` declares for the black box test does not exist there, and
`ok(err)` aborts the run before anything is instrumented. Type resolution
arrived in v1.3.4 (`09623a7`); v1.3.3 reports `Condition coverage: 1/2` on
the issue's minimal reproduction with Go 1.27.1, measured on 2026-10-08.

**What**: `export_test.go` is the usual Go idiom for handing an unexported
symbol to a package's black box tests: a file of `package x`, compiled only
into the test binary, that `x_test` reads. `go test` builds it and gobco
cannot: on `internal/tools/todos` it dies with
`action_specs_test.go:52:27: undefined: todos.PublishedActionIDs` before it
writes a single counter.

**How we found it**: the condition gate, first on `internal/clientcompat`
(pull request 1047) and then on `internal/tools/issues` (pull request 1067),
and its cause by reading `resolveTypes`. It was recorded in issue 1099 beside
entry 73's adoption until that issue closed on 2026-10-07.

### gobco bridges a black box test package through an import it may not find

- **Reported**: yes, by another user, as
  [rillig/gobco#33](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/issues/33) on
  2024-02-20, with a reproduction: a black box test that reaches its package
  only through a helper package. Read on 2026-10-27 it is open, with nine
  comments.
- **In review**: yes, by another contributor, as
  [rillig/gobco#39](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/39), opened on
  2026-05-21, which reads the import path from `go.mod` and the directory
  instead of from the imports. Read on 2026-10-27 it is open, last updated on
  2026-05-22.
- **Merged**: no. No gobco release has been tagged since v1.3.4 (2024-03-08).
- **Blocking**: no for the server. It kept the condition gate from measuring
  three packages until the workaround below: `internal/tools/awardemoji`,
  `internal/tools/freezeperiods` and `internal/tools/groupmarkdownuploads`,
  whose black box tests check the catalog's view of the package and import
  nothing of the package itself.
- **Workaround**: yes, since 2026-10-27, and temporary, by the maintainer's
  decision of that day that
  [entry 97](#gobco-cannot-instrument-a-package-whose-export_testgo-feeds-its-external-test-package)
  records. `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh`
  stages such a package and, in its copy of the module, adds a test file to
  the black box test package that imports the package and reads one name
  declared, for that file alone, in a file of the package behind
  `//go:build gc`, which the go command builds and gobco's narrower build
  context leaves uninstrumented. gobco then finds the import and writes a
  bridge that builds. The staging goes when gobco publishes a release carrying
  a fix, [rillig/gobco#39](https://github.com/rillig/gobco/pull/39) or
  another, and the pin of [entry 73](#gobco-type-checks-every-file-of-a-package-directory-whatever-its-build-constraints-say)
  moves to it.

**Where**: `rillig/gobco` at `v1.3.4`, `writeGobcoBlackBox`
(`instrumenter.go`). When a directory holds a package and its black box test
package, gobco writes `gobco_bridge_test.go`, which imports the package to
hand `GobcoCover` and `GobcoFinish` to the black box tests. It takes the
import path from an import whose name is the package's in any file of the
directory, and with none it writes the import with an empty path.

**What**: `go test` refuses the bridge at setup, so nothing is measured:

```text
gobco_bridge_test.go:3:9: invalid import path:
FAIL	github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/v3/internal/tools/freezeperiods [setup failed]
```

**How we found it**: the first whole-tree measurement, on 26 October 2026,
reported the three packages as not measured, and reading
`writeGobcoBlackBox` gave the cause.

### gobco drops GOPATH from its go test, which then reads another module cache

- **Reported**: no. Read on 2026-10-31, gobco's tracker has no issue about it.
- **In review**: no.
- **Merged**: no. No gobco release has been tagged since v1.3.4 (2024-03-08),
  and `master` at `7a09995`, read on 2026-10-31, drops the variable the same
  way.
- **Blocking**: no. Where `GOPATH` is the default, `$HOME/go`, as on CI's
  runners, the `go test` gobco runs reads the module cache the rest of the job
  reads. Where it names another directory, that `go test` reads the default
  cache instead, downloads every dependency it does not find there, and fails
  without the network, which is what running gobco from `PATH`
  ([issue 1515](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/issues/1515))
  is meant to need none of.
- **Workaround**: yes, since 2026-10-31, with the change for issue 1515:
  `scripts/coverage-conditions.sh` reads `GOMODCACHE` from `go env` and
  exports it to gobco, which passes every variable but `GOPATH` on, so its
  `go test` reads the cache `go mod download` filled whatever `GOPATH` says.
  It retires when a gobco release passes `GOPATH` on for a package in a
  module and the pin of
  [entry 73](#gobco-type-checks-every-file-of-a-package-directory-whatever-its-build-constraints-say)
  moves to it.

**Where**: `rillig/gobco` at `v1.3.4`, `goTest.env` (`main.go`, lines 458 to
478), and `master` at `7a09995` alike. `runGoTest` hands it no `GOPATH` for a
package in a module, and it then leaves `GOPATH` out of the environment of
the `go test` it runs; for a package in `GOPATH` mode it sets a `GOPATH` of
its own.

**What**: the go command takes the module cache from `GOMODCACHE`, and from
`GOPATH` as `$GOPATH/pkg/mod` when that is unset, so with `GOPATH` gone the
`go test` takes the cache below `$HOME/go`. The official `golang` image sets
`GOPATH=/go` with `HOME=/root`, and in it, with `/go/pkg/mod` filled and the
module proxy off, `GOPROXY=off gobco ./internal/config` fails before any test
runs:

```text
go: downloading github.com/joho/godotenv v1.5.1
# github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/v3/internal/config
env_file.go:40:2: module lookup disabled by GOPROXY=off
FAIL	github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/v3/internal/config [setup failed]
FAIL
go test ./internal/config: exit status 1
```

The same run with `GOMODCACHE=/go/pkg/mod` reports
`Condition coverage: 402/402`.

**How we found it**: checking the change for issue 1515 against the real go
and gobco, in that image: with gobco on `PATH` and the module proxy
unreachable, a run still failed, in the `go test` gobco runs, where every run
through `go run` had failed on the proxy before reaching it.

  no TryBot has run, and two things have moved. The reminder went up as a

  unmet now, a fourth unmet submit requirement. And Gerrit reports the change
  no longer mergeable into `master`:
  [go.dev/cl/847765](https://go.dev/cl/847765) ("go/types, types2: report
  error for oversized non-constant shift counts", `c8abe73e`, merged on
  2026-10-19) appended a test to the end of both `issues_test.go` files,
  where patch set 3 appends its own, so the patch no longer applies to
  either, while both `cycles.go` hunks still do;
  [go.dev/cl/854986](https://go.dev/cl/854986) ("go/types, types2: run some
  tests in parallel", `eeaa0945`, 2026-10-27) edited both test files again.
  Marking the reminder resolved in Gerrit clears the first, and a rebase of
  the pull request's branch onto `master`, force-pushed for GerritBot to
  import as patch set 4, the second; both are the maintainer's to post.
- **Merged**: no. No Go release carries a fix: go1.27.2 and go1.26.9,
  released on 2026-10-08, change nothing in either `cycles.go` (from go1.27.1
  to go1.27.2, go/types and types2 differ only in `named_test.go`, one line
  each), go1.27.3, released on 2026-10-19, changes nothing outside
  `crypto/x509`, and `master` still reads the field the same way. Read on
  2026-10-31, go1.27.3 is still the newest release, and neither `cycles.go`
  has changed on `master` since the change was uploaded.
- **Blocking**: no for the server, which type-checks nothing. It failed the
  race gate of a release rehearsal, in
  `TestAccess_OnlyTheSanctionedPackagesReadTheKey` of
  `internal/testutil/modelcorpus`, and any race run of a test that
  type-checks two or more packages in one go/packages load can fail the same
  way at random. Measured on 2026-09-29, 20 test packages did: the audits under
  `cmd/` that type-check Go source with go/packages, `cmd/internal/goprogram`,
  `cmd/internal/graphqldocs` and `internal/testutil/modelcorpus`. Read from
  the sources of `origin/main` on 2026-10-05, the packages added since that
  load programs in their tests are `cmd/gen_action_grants`, its
  `internal/derive` and `cmd/internal/actionrequests`, which belong on that
  list; `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/grants`, `cmd/gen_action_grants/internal/join`
  and `cmd/internal/sdkroutes` link go/packages only through the packages
  they import and load nothing, and neither does `cmd/audit_binary_vulns`,
  added on 2026-10-01. That is a reading of the
  sources, not the measurement of 2026-09-29, which has not been repeated.
- **Workaround**: yes. `internal/testutil/serialtypecheck` is imported blank by
  one test file of each of the 29 packages whose test binary links
  go/packages, counted on `origin/main` on 2026-10-05 (23 when this was last
  written, on 2026-10-01; the six since are those of the fine-grained grant
  derivation, `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/grants`, `cmd/gen_action_grants` with
  its `internal/derive` and `internal/join`, `cmd/internal/actionrequests`
  and `cmd/internal/sdkroutes`; 31 on 2026-10-13, the two since being
  `cmd/audit_edition_tier` and `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/required`, which reach
  go/packages through `cmd/internal/actionrequests` to read its committed
  record and load no program; 36 on 2026-10-31, the five since being
  `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/params`, `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/routes`,
  `cmd/audit_1to1/internal/sdkoptions`, `cmd/audit_i18n` and
  `cmd/audit_test_closed_servers`). In a race build its initializer sets
  GOMAXPROCS to one before go/packages sizes the semaphore it type-checks
  under, so the checkers run one after another; in any other build it changes
  nothing. Its tests hold
  the initialization order it relies on, and fail when a test binary links
  go/packages without it. Over fresh processes of the test that failed, the
  base raced in 13 of 80 and the workaround in 0 of 80. It retires when the Go
  release `go.mod` pins carries the fix: the package, its blank imports and
  its line in `TestDependencies_TestSupport_NeverReachesTheServerBinary` go
  together. Outside the detector the commands and their tests still
  type-check in parallel, and the read still races, with no effect on this
  tree. An instance expands from its origin's RHS, which for a type read from
  export data is its underlying type, and for every generic type this module
  and client-go v3.30.0, read on 2026-10-31, declare is a type literal. So `isComplete` returns
  true whichever value it reads (nil, the new type, or a torn pair of the
  two), which is its answer for any type no checker owns. What would change
  that is a generic type loaded from source whose RHS is another defined
  type, such as `type A[T any] B[T]`: a torn read of its instance
  dereferences a nil `*Named` and the command panics.

**Where**: `go/types` in go1.27.1, go1.27.2 and go1.27.3 (the file is the
same in all three), the last the toolchain `go.mod` pins since 2026-10-20,
and its copy
`cmd/compile/internal/types2`. `(*Checker).isComplete` reads `t.fromRHS` of a
`*Named` without unpacking it (`cycles.go:122`), while `(*Named).unpack`
expands an instance by writing `n.fromRHS = n.expandRHS()` (`named.go:244`).
go1.26 has the same unsynchronized read in `(*Checker).finiteSize`
(`cycles.go:127`, reached from `pendingType`), added with the value
observance check of CL 726580 and carried into `isComplete` by CL 734980 in
1.27. go1.25 has neither read. `hasVarSize` in `builtins.go` reads the same
field and unpacks first, with a comment saying why.

**What**: a package imported from export data is one `*types.Package` shared
by every checker that imports it, and the importer leaves a generic instance
reachable from its API unexpanded, for whichever checker needs it first to
expand. `iter.Seq[string]`, the result of `strings.SplitSeq`, is the one
these tests reach. Two checkers ranging over it race: one expands it through
`rangeKeyVal`, `commonUnder` and `Underlying`, the other reads the field in
`isComplete` from `callExpr`. go/packages type-checks every package it loads
from source in parallel, bounded by a semaphore sized from
`runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0)` when the package is initialized, so any load that
type-checks two packages from source is exposed. `GOMAXPROCS=1` set before
the process starts makes such a load serial and the race goes: 0 of 20 runs
against 2 of 20 at five. `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(1)` inside a test does nothing,
because the semaphore was sized before it ran. The report upstream says
go1.26 is not affected; a reproducer without x/tools, eight packages checked
concurrently against one imported `strings`, says it is: 30 of 30 runs
reported the race on go1.27.1, 10 of 30 on go1.26.8, and 0 of 30 on
go1.25.14.

**Fix upstream**: [golang/go#81871](https://github.com/golang/go/pull/81871)
([go.dev/cl/841585](https://go.dev/cl/841585)). `isComplete` returns true for
a `*Named` that no checker owns (`t.check == nil`) without reading its
`fromRHS`. Such a type comes from an importer, from the API or from a pass
that has finished, and its RHS cannot lead back to an object on this
checker's path, so the walk from it always ended in true:

```diff
 	case *Named:
+		if t.check == nil {
+			return true
+		}
 		obj = t.obj
 		rhs = t.fromRHS
```

On a toolchain built from `master` with the change, each of its test's two
subtests, run on its own, raced in none of 200 runs in each of `go/types`
and `types2`, where it raced in at least 99 of 100 without it. An instance
written as a type in the source is expanded before `Check` returns and does
not race; the source subtest uses one created by substitution
(`var F = Of[string]`), which stays unexpanded and unowned. The reproducer
went from 20 of 20 runs racing to none. A temporary assertion that the old
walk returns true for every such type held through `go build -a std cmd`,
`go vet std cmd` and both packages' tests.
Unpacking such a type first also removes the race: applied to both copies of
`cycles.go` on go1.27.1, it took the reproducer from 20 of 20 to 0 of 20 and
the test that failed here from about 3 in 40 to 0 in 40. But it expands the
instance only to reach an answer already known. Unpacking every named type
is wrong: it expands instances whose origin is still being checked, and
`TestFixedbugs/issue57522.go` panics with "nil typ" in `subst`.

**How we found it**: the race gate of a release rehearsal
(`.github/workflows/race.yml`, called by `release.yml`) failed in
`internal/testutil/modelcorpus`, and the report named two go/packages workers.
Reproducing it outside x/tools showed the read is in go/types and that
serializing the checkers is the only lever this side of the toolchain.
